plan.summary:
One plan, 7 waves, covering workstreams A to I. Workstream J returned an empty placeholder with no tasks or decisions, so its trust and data-protection items are not sequenced here; re-run the J design before Wave 1 ends.

Duplicates merged so nothing is built twice:
- A3 and C2 (agentic stream follow) are one task owned by A3.
- A7 folds into E4, and A8 folds into D10.
- G2 folds into H1 and H10, and F14 folds into G3.
- I14 folds into H9.
- G4's calendar view and the Microsoft calendar bundle fold into F3 and F5, and F5's reconnect union folds into G1.
- Three wall-clock and round-budget mechanisms (A4, C3, C4, B6, C5) collapse into one resolve_run_budget function plus one credential-expiry guard.

Wave outline:
- Wave 0 builds Do mode on gpt-5.6-terra dark behind one kill switch (A1) and closes the paid learning-review leak (A0). It also settles the compile, identity, Postgres and digest facts that gate later work. It needs no Terra quota.
- Wave 1 wires the built-but-unwired paths: plan grant plus persona, org and hook context in agentic runs; child-run registration; the scheduled-lane substrate; hosted-browser grants and a model planner on the user's route; working mail, calendar and file executor ops. It also includes the Office-first items that need no Do mode (H1, H2, H5).
- Wave 2 is the first Terra proof window, after the Codex reset on 2026-10-03 17:45 UTC, plus agent-path completion.
- Wave 3 closes B to F end to end.
- Waves 4 and 5 hold H (Office and data outputs), G (connector rows; reads in Wave 4, writes in Wave 5) and I (table stakes).
- Wave 6 is deferred.

Two flagged exceptions to the rule that G and I come after B to F:
- G1 is pulled into Wave 1 because it is a consent-correctness fix that F5 needs.
- I3 is pulled into Wave 1 because it stops launcher redeploys from killing in-flight Terra proof turns.

Three cross-cutting facts shape the whole plan:
- The 300 s delegated bearer bounds every A, B, C and E run.
- B's executing run cannot be proven on Terra under A's read-only rule unless effects are allowed on the proof stack with the ask posture.
- Six proto files and about ten hot source files are shared, so the ownership and ordering rules in file_conflicts are mandatory.

Convention: parallel_groups are listed in phase order. Tasks inside one group may touch the same hot file only in the disjoint functions named in file_conflicts. Additive-seam files take small re-read-before-edit hunks only. These are docker-compose.yml, gateway http_routes.rs, use-chat-controller.ts, ChatMessages.tsx, ChatPage.tsx, chat-types.ts and chat-normalizers.ts. Agents never commit, stash or revert.

waves.name: Wave 0 - Unblock proof, plug the paid leak, settle gating facts
waves.goal: Do mode (RunAgent) runs on gpt-5.6-terra via openai-codex-subscription behind one kill switch, built dark and proven with unit tests, e2e tests and free negative probes. The hidden paid learning-review call is closed. integration-corev2 owner-only tests compile, the plan-gate SQL runs on real Postgres, the template digest matches between BFF and Go, and the Terra planner schema probe is written. No Terra quota is needed. Groups are in phase order: A2 and A5 start after A1 lands, A3 and A4 after A2, and A6 last.
waves.exit_criteria:
A1 and the free probes:
- With the switch off, a Do request on the subscription route gets the typed 400 agentic_subscription_disabled and no run is created (A6 P1).
- With the switch on in the proof stack, a bogus subscription_connection_id ends with a typed subscription error. inference-core logs show no non-subscription provider for that request (A6 P2).
- Every RunAgent round of parent and child carries provider, connection and model. EXECUTION_AGENT_MODEL is ignored on a subscription run. A provider_used mismatch ends the run.

A0: capability-core logs show the learning-review consumer disabled on the proof stack, and a log check records whether it fired before.

A2 to A5: unit and e2e green.
- The paused-time test shows no 25 s tail after a finished run.
- Images build through the launcher model-plane-only copy (LAST_STACK_INDEX=2).
- cargo check of Data Plane v2 is clean after the execution.proto change, and Go wire-parity is green.

Other items:
- B10: plan-gate tests pass on a scratch Postgres database.
- D2: the golden digest vector passes in Rust and Go, and a goal containing '&' creates.
- F1: integration-corev2 internal/api compiles, the owner-only tests run, and the exchange probe result is recorded (400/401 means the grant is active, 403 means it is not).
- E3: the ignored test is written; its 3 to 5 Terra calls run in the first proof window.
- G12: the owner has started publisher verification.
waves.needs_owner: OD1 (snapshot shared WIP), OD2 (kill-switch default and effects posture), OD4 (learning review), OD5 (proof window), OD20 (frontend rebuild coordination). The owner starts G12 (publisher verification, external lead time) and decides OD16.

waves.name: Wave 1 - Wire the built-but-unwired paths (dark, unit and e2e proven)
waves.goal:
Fix what exists but is not end to end:
- Plan grant, persona, org and hook context in agentic runs: B1, B3, B4, B8.
- Child-run registration, durable lineage cards, research-only child tools: C1, C7, C8.
- Scheduled-lane substrate (policy, run profile, result persistence, truthful status, 'Varsle meg', read-boundary fix): D1, D3, D5, D6, D9, D12.
- Hosted-browser grants, broker policy, planner on the user's route, risk classifier: E1, E2, E4, E6, E7.
- Mail, calendar and file executor ops plus an additive consent path: F2, F3, F4, F5, G1.
- Office-first items needing no Do mode: H1, H2, H5.
- Redeploy-safe turns: I3.

Nothing is switched on by default. Groups are in phase order.
waves.exit_criteria:
- Unit and e2e suites pass for every task.
- Images are built only through the launcher. Model plane uses LAST_STACK_INDEX=2; BFF, imports and ingestion use their own stages. The frontend container is restarted only after a git status check; otherwise verify on :5199.
- Data Plane v2 cargo check is clean after each proto batch.

Model-free live proofs:
- B1: the plan grant reads back after a model-gateway restart.
- E1 and E2: a hosted-browser run with a broker-issued grant starts and completes on the deterministic planner, with no 403 and no model call.
- C1: the probe shows user-bearer registration accepted and records whether the service token was refused.
- D1: the readiness script reports every binding present. The owner applies the policy.
- F2 to F4: httptest suites green and integration-corev2 builds.
- H1: real Excel and PowerPoint fixtures extract correctly (formulas, dates, notes).
- E6: a dated record of tabs, DevTools and replay.
- I3: model-gateway drains in-flight streams on SIGTERM.
waves.needs_owner: OD1 (snapshot before C7, D1 and C8 start), OD6 (plan-gate defaults), OD9 (D1 apply timing), OD13 (E2 and E4 domain scope and planner route), OD10 (F-chain defaults).

waves.name: Wave 2 - First Terra proof window and agent-path completion
waves.goal:
After the Codex window resets (owner memory: 2026-10-03 17:45 UTC; confirm with one canary turn), run the Do-on-Terra proofs (A6 P3 to P5) that unblock B, C and F. Also run the queued W0 and W1 live proofs from the proof ladder: E3, H5, H1, H2.

Then finish the agent paths:
- Plan approval starts the executing run, with step recitation, durable receipts and a round budget.
- Wide-research budgets, breaker and gateway clamps.
- The agent mail, file and calendar read tool with untrusted-content handling.
- The scheduled agent step, notifications and results UI.
- Browser run live proof and answer-in-thread.
- The picker chain proven on Terra.

Code work continues before the reset; proofs are queued.
waves.exit_criteria:
A6 P3 to P5 on Terra:
- Tool steps and an answer on a Do turn.
- A plan_proposed frame.
- A 3-item fan-out with attach and stop events.
- Dated evidence of zero requests to any non-subscription provider and no cost ledger rows.

B2, B5 and B9:
- An approved plan starts the executing run from the web app.
- Steps are recited and ticked.
- The proof bundle names the plan id and rung.
- Live proof of the executing run needs effects allowed on the proof stack with the ask posture (OD2). Use a read-only 2 to 3 step plan.

C3 to C5:
- Fan-out items get a real round budget.
- The org clamp shows 3 of 6 items run.
- The breaker is proven by mocked tests only.

F6 and F8:
- read_provider_action never pauses for approval, which settles the capability-gate finding.
- Session-core step records hold no mail or file text.

Other items:
- F10: the picker chain on Terra passes the design's assertions.
- E5: the Terra planner takes at least two non-observe actions. The login gate is approved and denied. The honest-failure path shows no silent Observe loop.
- D4, D7 and D8: unit and Postgres proven.
- If Terra reports a cap, stop and record it. Never switch model.
waves.needs_owner: OD2 (effects on proof stack), OD3 (quota numbers), OD5 (proof window), OD7 (child budget design), OD10 (autonomous own-data reads), OD12 (proof accounts connected by the owner), OD13 (hosted-browser rules).

waves.name: Wave 3 - Close B to F end to end
waves.goal:
Finish the large items and record the proofs:
- Plan continuation after an approval pause.
- Wide-research entry point and cards that survive reload.
- Longer run credentials, only if measurement demands it.
- Unattended owner identity for scheduled runs, behind a security gate, then the scheduled-run proof on Terra.
- Browser bridge from /chat with live view and takeover.
- Office-file text for the agent.
- The shared-inbox ownership model.
- Dated evidence rows in the gap plan.

G and I work may start only after Wave 2 exit is met and Wave 3 group 1 is merged.
waves.exit_criteria:
- B7: a manual 'Fortsett planen' continues a plan after an approval pause.
- C6 and C7: the 'Bred forskning' toggle sends a clamped request and the cards survive a reload.
- C9: built only if OD8 says yes and the security review passes.
- C10: a 6-item Terra run proves child registration, lineage, reload and no budget-Exhausted. It records p50 item time to set the OD3 numbers.
- D10: passes adversarial review before activation.
- D13: a scheduled run on Terra proves the notification, the result drawer, the failure cases and zero Balance spend.
- E9 and E10: from a chat answer, open the hosted browser, watch steps, approve a gate, take over and hand back.
- F13: the eight checks pass, including delegated reads without approval pauses.
- F11b: enforces owner-only for personal connections in the shared inbox.
- G16: compliance drafts recorded as pending counsel.
- B11: the executing-run proof is recorded.
- Gap-plan rows are updated only with observed evidence.
waves.needs_owner: OD5 (D10 go/no-go and security review), OD8 (credential lifetime), OD11 (shared inbox), OD13, OD15 (policy batch applied by the owner through the Control launcher), OD12.

waves.name: Wave 4 - Office and data outputs, read-side connector rows, chat-core quick wins
waves.goal:
Owner priority is Office documents first. Ship:
- Direct PDF, charts in Office exports, staged data in the sandbox, local OCR, and xlsx/pptx in knowledge.
- The read-side connector rows: Excel and Sheets range read and attach, Office-file sync built dark.
- Hosted-browser prod parity.
- Small chat-core table stakes that also fix silent wrong behaviour: shortcuts, idempotency key, streaming render, citation binding, skill picks on Terra, supersede and branch, search, templates, usage meter, and the reasoning spike.

Gate: Wave 2 exit met and Wave 3 group 1 merged.

- H3: a real PDF downloads from a Terra answer with no print dialog and no window.print call.
- H4: exports open in real Word, Excel and PowerPoint with no repair prompt.
- H6: pandas totals match a Python reference.
- H9: local OCR finishes inside the 18 s BFF budget.

- I6: citation chips bind by number.

- I8: a branch carries server-side history.

waves.name: Wave 5 - Writes, designed deck path, deeper chat core
waves.goal:
G rows that write start only after reads are proven. Order of work:
- Always-ask in front of every provider write.
- The human-click apply path.
- Calendar and sheet proposal cards.
- Save-to-cloud.
- Edit-in-place for Office files.

- Heavier chat-core items: restart orphan settling, server-side versions, rewind, canvas phase 1.
waves.exit_criteria:
- Every write goes through human approval plus a signed attestation. Always-ask is proven by unit tests, and the click path is proven live on Terra.
- Terra generates an xlsx and one click saves it to OneDrive and Drive, with a receipt and verified read-back. A second click is idempotent. A stale-eTag replace returns 409.
- A calendar event and a sheet-range proposal are applied by click on Terra. The card shows conflicts or before/after. Attendees are refused in v1. A =WEBSERVICE formula is refused.
- The admin-wall card and consent sheet are proven on the business test tenant.
- Do-mode agent writes are proven by mocks only.
- G15 contacts stay off until counsel signs.
- G6 edit-in-place passes the real-Excel check.
- H8 passes the COM open check with no repair prompt.

waves.goal: Parked, each with a revisit trigger.

No work in this wave. Revisit triggers:

plan.critical_path:
Build chain:
1. A1 (RunAgent route, kill switch, proto number ledger) to A2 and A4 to A3 to the A6 free probes.
2. The Terra reset gate at 2026-10-03 17:45 UTC.
3. A6 live P3 to P5.
4. The B11, C10 and F13 proofs.

Longest serial lane, the execution-core agent.rs and mod.rs seams: A1, A2, A4, C1, C8, B4, B3, C3, C4, B5, F6, F8, G8. Put new logic in new modules to shorten it.

Other long poles:
- D3 to D4 (L) to D10 (L, adversarial security-review gate) to D13.
- E2 and E1 to E4 to E8 to E9 to E10 (L).
- B1 to B2 and B5 (L) to B7 (L).
- Gate for G writes: F6, F8 and F13 proven, then G1, G7, G8, G9, G13 and G14.

Quota gate: every live proof shares one Codex account window, which was exhausted on 2026-09-29. Proof ladder after a one-turn canary:
1. A6 P3 to P5.
2. H5 (five turns).
3. F10 (about 10 Ask turns).
4. E3, then E5 (about 25 to 30 calls).
5. H1 and H2 turns.
6. B11, C10, F13 and D13.

This totals roughly 150 Terra calls, so spread it across windows by priority. If a cap is hit, record it and stop; never switch model.

Hard ceiling: the 300 s delegated bearer. A runs about 270 s. B plan runs need 4+3n rounds at 10 to 40 s each, so even a 3-step plan overruns the 240 s clamp on Terra. B7's manual continuation or OD8's longer bearer decides whether B is useful on Terra. Wide research is capped at 6 to 8 items on Terra without OD8.

owner_decisions.question: Snapshot the uncommitted shared work before Wave 1: untracked research_fan_out.rs and ChatWideResearchPanel.tsx, the delegated-identity files (auth-core plane-token.controller.ts, plane-service-principals.json, run-control-plane.sh, integration-corev2 auth files) and regenerated pb.go files? Agents never commit, stash or revert.
owner_decisions.options: Owner commits or makes a WIP snapshot first / continue in the working tree
owner_decisions.recommended: Snapshot now. First confirm the real checkout is C:/dev/CoresSystem (the session cwd is not a git repo, and OneDrive near-duplicates exist) and scan for NUL-filled files. One more abrupt shutdown would lose the untracked files.
owner_decisions.blocks: C3, C4, C7, C8, D1, D10, F1 step 5, F7, E11, every proto batch

owner_decisions.question: Enable Do mode on the ChatGPT subscription route (AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_ENABLED), may it run effects, and should a test-only stub route exist? (Merges A's two decisions, the Do-mode test-route questions from E, F, G and C, and B11's need for an executing run.)
owner_decisions.options: Switch off everywhere / on only in the proof stack / on by default. Read-only (plan_mode forced) / effects with ask posture. Stub route or none.
owner_decisions.recommended: Code and compose default OFF; ON only in the proof stack for A6. Read-only for the first proof, enforced server-side. Allow effects on the proof stack only when B's executing-run proof needs it: AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_ALLOW_EFFECTS, ask posture, per-call approvals, and B1 accepting execute_plan_id on subscription only then (B1's design refuses it, which would make B11 impossible). Flip the compose default after the dated live proof and your acceptance. No stub route: the real subscription path is exercised and the free negative probes cover the rest.
owner_decisions.blocks: A1 enablement, A5 UI, A6 live, B11, C10, F13, E12, G Do-mode paths

owner_decisions.question: Quota guard and run budgets for Do runs and wide research on the subscription route (the plan hit its usage cap on 2026-09-29).
owner_decisions.options: Rounds 4 / 8-10 / more; fan-out concurrency 2 / 3 / 4; one Do run in flight per user; wide ceiling 24 or 100
owner_decisions.recommended: First proof: rounds 10 for the whole run (parent plus children), fan-out concurrency 2, wall clock 240 s, one Do run in flight per user. Then rounds 8 and concurrency 3. Wide-research defaults, all env-tunable and replaced after C10 measures: ceiling 24 items (hard cap 100), 4 rounds per item (cap 6), at most 400 child rounds, parent max_rounds 6, breaker after 3 provider failures, 3-wide on subscription and 4 on metered. Raise the subscription round cap on the proof stack for B11 only, because plan runs need 12 or more rounds.

owner_decisions.question: May the background skill-learning review send a subscription-route run's transcript to a paid model (it calls claude-sonnet-4-5 with a service credential today)?
owner_decisions.options: Never / only on the user's own route / yes
owner_decisions.recommended: Never. Disable it on the proof stack now (A0). Permanent rule: skip any thread that ran on a user-owned subscription route until the review can run on that user's own route with a delegated credential. It is both a standing-rule leak and a data-protection issue.

owner_decisions.question: Terra proof window and quota spend: confirm the Codex reset, approve the proof ladder, and allow a refresh of the local test sign-in (needed after a reboot).
owner_decisions.options: One window / split across windows by priority / wait
owner_decisions.recommended: Canary turn first to confirm the reset (owner memory says 2026-10-03 17:45 UTC). Then run the ladder in the critical_path order and spread about 150 calls across windows by priority. If capped mid-proof, record the cap and stop; never switch model or use Verevon Balance.
owner_decisions.blocks: Every live proof (A6 P3-P5, E3, E5, F10, H1, H2, H5, B11, C10, D13, F13)

owner_decisions.question: Plan-gate defaults (B): does approval pre-authorize effects, does Approve auto-start the run, how does the plan continue after an approval pause, what is the round budget, what is recited, and where do hooks apply?
owner_decisions.options: (1) Rung only caps, each effect still asks / (2) pre-authorize kept operations / (3) pre-authorize all within the rung. Auto-start or a 'Kjor planen' button. Manual or automatic continuation. Plan-derived rounds or a global raise. Approved-plan recitation only or a model todo. Hooks on the agentic loop only or the inline loop too. Inline plan gate or wait.
owner_decisions.recommended: Option 1 (each effectful action still asks). Auto-start with a visible user message, and keep the button as the retry and reload state. Manual 'Fortsett planen' in v1. Plan-derived rounds for plan runs only. Recite the approved plan only. Hooks on the governed agentic loop only (record the ruling in docs/decisions/ledger.md). No inline plan gate; wait for Do on Terra.
owner_decisions.blocks: B1 normalize behaviour, B2, B4, B6, B7

owner_decisions.question: Wide-research design (C): budget semantics, entry point, who may use it and the org limit.
owner_decisions.options: Pool from parent rounds with a raised ceiling / separate child budget with even division kept / leave as is. Composer toggle without a confirm / with a confirm step / model-chosen only.
owner_decisions.recommended: Separate child budget, even division kept, parent charged 0 rounds. A composer toggle in Do mode with 12/24/48 presets and no confirm gate in v1. All non-ZDR members may use it. The org admin may set max_subagents_per_run; unset means 24 on wide turns and 8 otherwise. WIDE_RESEARCH_FAN_OUT_ENABLED stays the deployment kill switch. The honest Terra ceiling is 6 to 8 items without OD8.

owner_decisions.question: Run-length credential: allow a longer-lived delegated bearer class (up to 1500 s, hard cap 1800 s) beyond the 300 s default? Generalised from C9; the same 300 s ceiling bounds A, B, C and E.
owner_decisions.options: Wide-research turns only / every agentic, plan and browser run / keep 300 s
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes for wide-research turns only, after a short security review, and only if C10 or B11 show real runs crossing 240 s. Do not generalise yet. Otherwise accept 6 to 8 items on Terra and use B7's manual continuation for plans.
owner_decisions.blocks: C9, C4 window checks, B7 and B11 viability, E run length

owner_decisions.question: Scheduled runs (merges A's and D's decisions): when to apply the scheduled-lane policy (D1), may a scheduled step act as the schedule owner on the subscription route (D10), what may it read, where does the owner see the result, what are the cadence and failure rules, and what is the notification surface? A8 is folded into D10.
owner_decisions.options: Apply now / after D4 merges / not at all. Token exchange bound to the Control decision (a) / inference-core verifies the decision itself (b) / no owner identity (c). Web only / plus knowledge / plus personal connectors. Read-only transcript plus 'Fortsett i chat' / user-owned delivery thread. Bell with link only / preview / push or email. Fail visibly / fall back to a managed model.

D10 via option (a): limited to inference-core, 120 s, subscription route only, with an adversarial security review before activation. v1 reads web only and stays draft-only: a read-only tool allowlist, and a NeedsApproval step fails the run. The owner reads the result through the personal-Space transcript plus 'Fortsett i chat'. Floor of 1 hour for non-admins, 10 active schedules per creator, auto-pause after 3 consecutive failures, 'Kjor na' once per 10 minutes. The bell shows title and link only. Fail visibly with no fallback to Balance. No scheduled run spends a personal plan until D10 ships.

owner_decisions.question: Agent reads of personal data (F): may the agent read the run owner's own mail, files and calendar without a per-call approval? Also ZDR, egress after flagged content, Ask-mode tools, the imports:extract scope, the calendar scope path and a SharePoint picker tab.

SharePoint picker tab now or not.

Refuse ZDR. Do not build F12. Before any customer org uses it, require approval for egress tools after a Flagged read (F8b). imports:extract only on the extract path, never imports:write. Calendar through the connect path only, not sign-in. No SharePoint picker tab now.

owner_decisions.question: Shared inbox vs owner-only personal connections. Today emailsync polls personal Microsoft and Google connections into an org-wide inbox that inbox_search and the Inbox UI show to every member. This contradicts the owner-only ruling.
owner_decisions.options: (a) keep org-wide / (b) connection visibility 'personal' or 'org' with an explicit share choice at connect time / (c) tag conversations with their owner and filter
owner_decisions.recommended: (b), with existing inbox connections switched to org only on your say-so. Interim: stop syncing personal-provider connections into the shared inbox unless they are explicitly shared. Until then, state that inbox_* is org-wide and do not point F6 at it.
owner_decisions.blocks: F11b, F11a copy, F13 negative test

owner_decisions.question: Accounts and tenants for live proof of connectors, writes and consent. OAuth consent is an owner action.
owner_decisions.options: Dedicated test accounts / production mailboxes
owner_decisions.recommended: A dedicated Microsoft 365 developer tenant with a SharePoint site and Sites.Read.All consented, plus a dedicated Gmail account, seeded with fixed fixtures. For G11, a business test tenant with the default consent policy, one non-admin member and one admin. Never production mailboxes.
owner_decisions.blocks: F10, F13, G4 and G5 live, G11, G13, G14

owner_decisions.question: Hosted-browser run rules (E): domain scope and who owns the policy, whether the answer is written into the thread, whether the planner may run on the user's subscription, how the user owns the agent's Quarry run, and the planner default.
owner_decisions.options: Fence of start host plus listed domains / plus an org allow-list / open web with a deny-list. Write the answer to the thread / keep it in the panel. Planner on the subscription when selected / Balance only. User's delegated quarry bearer / service principal with a broker proof. QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM default on or off.
owner_decisions.recommended: A hard fence of the start host plus domains the user lists, with the broker as policy authority (deny-list, at most 8 domains). Write the planner's result and source URLs into the thread, non-ZDR only, never raw page text. The planner may run on the user's subscription only when that route is selected; the default stays verevon-balance for everyone else. Run the agent with the user's delegated aud=quarry bearer, which is bounded by the 300 s lifetime and the 240 s clamp. Keep QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM default OFF in compose until E5 passes, so no manual AI-loop run silently moves to the paid planner. The user's own Chrome is never used.

owner_decisions.options: Always ask every write / ask once per chat for creates / trusted after N clean runs. No attendees in v1 / with a second confirm / freely. CROSS-CUTTING RISKS:
- 300 s bearer: it bounds A (270 s deadline), E (240 s clamp), C, and B's executing runs. Plan runs need 4+3n rounds at 10 to 40 s each, so even a 3-step plan overruns the 240 s clamp on Terra. A mis-sized proof will look like a failure.
- Quota: one Codex account hit its cap on 2026-09-29. There is no preflight meter on the subscription route, because cost-core counts it as 0. The proof ladder is about 150 calls.
- Emulated tool JSON: nested arrays in plan.propose and plan.step_status can fail to parse on Terra. Measure the first-attempt parse rate in A6 and B11. Terra may also under-elect tools (tool_choice auto); add a required first-round tool_choice behind a flag if live runs show zero tool calls.
- Rollout order: an old execution-core ignores the new proto fields and would run the loop on model-router (paid). Enable the switch only after the new execution-core image is confirmed running. inference-core's 'agentic' capability follows the same variable. An A-side route echo from execution-core would catch a mis-ordered rollout.
- Shared dirty tree: many files carry other sessions' uncommitted edits. Never stash or revert. Regenerate pb files with tooling. Scan for NUL bytes after any reboot. The session cwd is not a git repo; the real checkout is C:/dev/CoresSystem (verify .git, beware OneDrive near-duplicates).
- Build only through the launcher. Frontend rebuilds restart the container serving live source (OD20).
- Capability gate: finding F3 (name-only HIGH capability makes every execute_provider_action ask) is from reading code, not observed. F13 settles it. cap.tool.provider.read and execute are source_only in the promotion ledger.
- Unverified assumptions to confirm early:
  - user tokens carry orchestration:write (B1 seed);
  - Session Core accepts a child-run bearer (C1 probe);
  - ExecuteStep accepts steps on a completed run (G9 spike; run the no-model spike in Wave 3 to de-risk Wave 5);
  - Graph and Google behaviours in F2, F3 and G7.
- J: the design returned no tasks. Re-run it. Its owner-only list (external audit, pentest, counsel review, Postmark account, cross-tenant spec, captions) is unsequenced here. The Postmark self-forward mail-to-task Phase 1 from the 2026-09-28 owner rulings needs a Wave 1 or 2 slot once J is designed.

owner_decisions.question: Does approving a plan pre-authorize the plan's effectful actions, or does each effectful action still ask? (Today the executing run keeps the 'ask' posture, so every risky tool pauses even after the plan and rung were approved.)
owner_decisions.options: (1) Each effectful action still asks, rung only caps what may be attempted. (2) A danger_full_access approval pre-authorizes steps whose operation slug the user kept in the plan, run under auto posture for those operations only. (3) Approval pre-authorizes everything within the rung.
owner_decisions.recommended: Option 1. It is the current, tested behaviour and the safest; B7 removes the stall it causes. Revisit option 2 only after live runs show the extra prompts are the main friction.

owner_decisions.question: Should Approve start the executing run automatically?
owner_decisions.options: Auto-start with a visible user message, or a separate 'Kjør planen' button.
owner_decisions.recommended: Auto-start, with the button kept as the retry and reload state (B2). The approval is already the explicit confirm gate and the transcript shows an honest user turn.

owner_decisions.question: After an approval-gated action runs, should the plan continue automatically or on a click (B7)?
owner_decisions.options: Manual 'Fortsett planen' button, or an automatic server-side continuation run after the delivery worker settles.
owner_decisions.recommended: Manual in v1. Automatic continuation needs a server trigger on the worker's outcome and a fresh run per approval; size it separately after the manual flow is used live.

owner_decisions.question: Round budget for executing runs (B6) and the global Do cap of 4.
owner_decisions.options: Plan-derived budget for plan runs only, or also raise every Do run to execution-core's own default of 12.
owner_decisions.recommended: Plan-derived for plan runs only in this workstream; the global raise is a cross-workstream call because wide research edits the same literal.

owner_decisions.question: Checklist recitation for plan-less Do runs (a model-written todo list, Manus todo.md style).
owner_decisions.options: Seed recitation only from an approved plan (v1), or also let the model keep its own todo list in every Do run.
owner_decisions.recommended: Approved plan only in v1; add a model-written todo only if live runs show plan-less long runs drifting.

owner_decisions.question: Do org hook rules also have to apply to the inline gateway loop's tools?
owner_decisions.options: Agentic loop only (B4), or also the inline loop.
owner_decisions.recommended: Agentic only. apps/Model Plane/CLAUDE.md keeps the two dispatch loops separate on purpose, and inline tools on the Terra route are read-only builtins. Record the ruling in docs/decisions/ledger.md.

owner_decisions.question: Run the plan gate on the inline loop so it can be proven on Terra today?
owner_decisions.options: Build a gateway-side plan.propose and approved-plan injection for Ask turns, or wait for Do mode on Terra.
owner_decisions.recommended: Wait for Do mode on Terra. Inline tools have no effects to gate, so a plan gate there would add a visible plan but control nothing, and it would add a second implementation of the gate.

risks: Live proof is blocked on Do mode: every B capability exists only in the agentic path, execution-core hard-codes an empty subscription_connection_id (agent.rs:1070) and normalize.rs:186-206 rejects agentic and plan_mode on the subscription route. B11 and every live proof depends on the Do-on-Terra workstream (assumed A). What can be proven now: B10 real-Postgres tests, the unit and e2e suites, BFF strip behaviour.

Proto field-number and file collisions with other workstreams: RunAgentRequest already has max_subagents = 15 uncommitted, and Do-on-Terra and wide research will add fields. This plan reserves 20 (authored_instructions), 21 (hook_context), 22 (approved_plan) and leaves 16-19 to others; spawn_run_dispatch (max_rounds, max_subagents, subscription fields) is edited by several workstreams, so split the RunAgentRequest literal into a pure builder early (B4) to make merges mechanical. Proto changes need buf generate for the checked-in Go pb files and updates to mp-orchestration proto_shim.rs and the proto_wire_parity tests in Rust and Go.

Other sessions have uncommitted edits in the very files B2 touches (use-chat-controller.ts, ChatMessages.tsx, chat-types.ts, ChatPage.tsx, DashboardComposer.tsx) and in Model Plane sse.rs, http_routes.rs, coordinator.rs, plan.rs, agent.rs, orchestration protos and regenerated Go files. Never commit, stash or revert; re-read before every edit; the frontend container serves live source with no hot reload, so restart it only after checking git status.

Approval-gated tools end the loop and the durable continuation path is a stub (execution-core grpc.rs:691): even with B7 the continuation is a fresh run with only the goal, the plan block and the original request, not the in-run context. Until B7 ships, an approved plan with an effectful step stops at that step.

An agentic run starts with a fresh history (agent.rs:956-972): it does not see earlier turns, attachments, memory or the date. B1 carries the original request and B3 the instructions, but prior-conversation context is not passed; that is a pre-existing design property to take to the owner if plan quality suffers.

Reload relinking: SetRunMode flips the plan run to mode 'execute' and hydrateLatestPlanRun relinks only mode 'plan' runs, so an approved-not-started plan may not be restored after a reload unless B2 step 5 is done. Verify it in the Playwright test, not by reading.

Gateway restarts: the in-memory grants map stays as a write-only cache for one release; the durable record is authoritative from B1. Two tabs clicking 'Kjør planen' at once: the compare-and-swap lets one claim win and the other get plan_claim_failed, but two continuations of an already-EXECUTING plan are not serialized (the SPA disables the button while streaming).

Terra-specific: plan.propose and plan.step_status take nested JSON arguments and the subscription route emulates tool calls; a malformed first attempt costs a full retry. Measure the first-attempt parse rate in B11 before declaring the gate usable on Terra.

B8 can mislead the model if a read-back is wrong; the verifiers fail open to Inconclusive by design. The audit records no real Outlook, Gmail, Visma or other provider connection ever exercised, so B8's value is unproven until a connector workstream lands.

Model-managed checklists drift: a model that never calls plan.step_status leaves every item unticked, and the recitation then nags; the plan also stays EXECUTING, so B7's button must key on the run outcome (awaiting_approval, failed or exhausted), not on 'plan not COMPLETED'.

Services to rebuild: model-gateway, execution-core, session-core, the BFF gateway (strip rules) and the frontend container. Build only through apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/build-verevon-services.sh; a model-plane-only copy with LAST_STACK_INDEX=2 avoids restarting the frontend for B1, B3, B4, B5, B6, B8 and B9. Hand-built docker compose builds miss the Control Plane env chain.

Unverified in this read-only pass: whether a user session token carries orchestration:write for a ProposePlan seed in the live script; the exact Arbeidsplan card lines in ChatPanels.tsx; whether run.mode 'execute' is read by any consumer after approval. Each is called out where it matters.
designs.live_proof: Rule: live tests run only on gpt-5.6-terra via openai-codex-subscription, never on Verevon Balance or any paid provider. Every B capability lives in the agentic (Do) path, which is disabled on the subscription route (DashboardComposer.tsx:1268 subscriptionBacked check, chat-client.ts:1029, normalize.rs:186-206, execution-core agent.rs:1070), so the end-to-end proof CANNOT be run live until Do mode works on Terra (assumed workstream A). No paid-balance fallback is proposed. WHAT CAN BE PROVEN NOW, with no model call: (1) B10 real-Postgres suite on a scratch database (compare-and-swap, supersede, reorder, claim, step transitions, set_run_mode grant metadata, approvals plan binding); (2) unit and mocked e2e suites for every task (RunAgentRequest captured by the mock execution server shows goal, autonomy_rung, authored_instructions, hook_context, approved_plan, max_rounds); (3) BFF strip tests; (4) optionally, a model-free durability check: send one ordinary Terra Ask turn to get a thread and run id, seed a PROPOSED plan on that thread (only if a ProposePlan call with the test user's own session credential is permitted), approve it through the BFF plan-approval route, restart model-gateway, and read the plan (APPROVED) and the plan run's metadata (autonomy_rung, approved_plan_id, autonomy_granted_at) back through the gateway; this shows the grant survives a restart. WHEN DO MODE RUNS ON TERRA (B11), record with content-free evidence (ids, states, counts; never prompt text or secrets): set the persona to 'Svar alltid på nynorsk' and add a Space instruction; send a Do turn with a 4-step goal on Terra; confirm the plan card shows steps, edit a title, remove one, add one, approve at workspace_write with a justification; confirm the 'Utfør den godkjente planen' turn starts by itself; confirm the final answer is in nynorsk and follows the Space rule (B3); confirm the edited steps, not the originals, drive the run and each step ticks in the Arbeidsplan card (B5); restart model-gateway between approve and start in a second run and confirm it still starts (B1); confirm the proof bundle for the executing run names the plan id and rung (B9); register a deny hook for a risky tool and confirm the refusal in the trace (B4); count 'invalid subscription tool arguments' events during the run to size the Terra tool-call risk. B6 (budget), B7 (continuation) and B8 (verification) additionally need an effectful tool with a real connection and cannot be proven live until a connector is exercised on Terra.

designs.workstream: A. Agentic runs on the Terra route (unblocks live proof for B, C, F and parts of D, E)
designs.goal: Make Do mode (execution-core RunAgent: plan mode, wide research, the agent's connector tools) run on gpt-5.6-terra over openai-codex-subscription, with a kill switch, so B, C, F and parts of D and E can be proven live under the standing rule (Terra subscription route only, never Verevon Balance or any paid provider). Verdict: feasible, about M+M plus small follow-ups. No test-only route is needed, because inference-core's unary Infer already emulates tool calls over the subscription (codex_subscription_tools.rs prepare/parse, max 16 calls per round) and execution-core's loop only uses unary Infer. Two parts do not fit this slice: scheduled runs (A8, needs an owner decision and a delegated identity) and the browser planner (A7, waits for F).
designs.current_state:
All of this is by reading the working tree (several of these files carry other sessions' uncommitted edits); nothing was run. Do mode is blocked at six layers, and the first four must all change.

1. Composer. apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/DashboardComposer.tsx: `subscriptionBacked` memo (L1001-1003) feeds `planMode` (L1268), and the Ask/Do control is `disabled={subscriptionBacked() || conversationOnly()}` (L2953, L2990).
2. Wire builder. src/shared/api/chat-client.ts buildChatWireBody: `agentic` is dropped (L1029) and `plan_mode` forced false (L1057) for the subscription provider.
3. Model-gateway normalize. apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/normalize.rs L183-206 returns 400 if a subscription request carries `plan_mode` or the `agentic` feature. The same rule also rejects zdr, attachments, browse_web, deep_research, generate_image, client tools and a structured schema; those must stay rejected.
4. Dispatch drops the route. The gateway's agentic branch (sse.rs L1142-1200) never passes `provider_hint` or `subscription_connection_id`, and `RunAgentRequest` (proto/model_plane/v1/execution.proto L76-180) has no field for them. `spawn_run_dispatch` (sse.rs L8331-8425) sends `max_rounds: 4` (L8380) and `max_subagents: 0` (L8424).
5. execution-core refuses on purpose. agent.rs run_rounds sets `provider_hint: String::new()` and `subscription_connection_id: String::new()` (L1053, L1072), with the comment "Governed agent loops cannot select a user-owned ChatGPT subscription". `resolve_agent_model` (L2781) swaps in `EXECUTION_AGENT_MODEL`, and compose sets that to `model-router` by default (apps/Model Plane/deploy/docker-compose.yml ~L938). So even with the plumbing, the loop would run on the paid Azure router.
6. Error typing is lost. An Infer failure becomes `RoundsOutcome::InferFailed` (L1086-1102) and then the generic reply "I wasn't able to complete that request right now". A `subscription_usage_limit` or reauth refusal never reaches the user, and the gateway's Failed arm (sse.rs L8898-8911) emits a generic `agent_run_failed`.

What already works on this route and can be reused:
- The inline chat tool loop (tool_loop.rs ~L6638-6750) already runs tool rounds on the subscription and checks `provider_used`/`model_used` fail-closed.
- inference-core's chain never fails over from a subscription (fallback.rs L1209-1219 and the test at L2280).
- The Infer bearer execution-core already holds is user-bound (auth.rs `authenticate_delegated_inference`, L422-438), so Integration Core's org/user ownership check on the connection passes for the owner's own connection.
- Typed refusals arrive on gRPC trailers `x-mp-provider-error`, `x-mp-retry-after-ms`, `x-mp-resets-at`.
- Children (`subagent.task` and `research_fan_out`) copy the parent `req` and `agent_model` (agent.rs L2544-2571), so a route stored once on the request reaches every child.
- The broker limits are 16 concurrent calls globally and 4 per connection, with a 30 s queue (integration-corev2/internal/codexsubscription/limiter.go).

Defects found along the way that matter on a slow route:
- Gateway stream timing. agentic_run_stream tails orchestration events until 25 s of silence (sse.rs L8672-8681, no break on a terminal event). Session-core's tail is a broadcast with no end and no keepalive (orchestration_grpc.rs L3173-3232). It then waits only 30 s for the RunAgent result (L8688-8689). Consequences: every Do turn pays up to ~25 s of idle after it finishes, and a Terra run (each round is a Codex process, 10-40 s) that is silent for more than ~55 s gets "agent_dispatch_unavailable" while the run keeps going server-side.
- Round budget. `max_rounds` 4 is shared by the parent and all children (agent.rs L1020), so no more than 4 Infer calls happen per run.
- Token lifetime. Per-audience tokens default to 300 s (auth-core convex-token.service.ts), so a run must not start new rounds after about 240 s.
- No metering. Do runs record no tokens or cost anywhere (grep finds no usage envelope in execution-core, and the gateway's usage frame is hard-coded 0). On Terra, quota burn is invisible.
- Hidden paid call. capability-core's skill-learning consumer reviews every non-ZDR completed run with `LEARNING_REVIEW_MODEL` defaulting to `claude-sonnet-4-5` (compose ~L1283; go/services/capability-core/cmd/main.go L750-767; sessionreview/consumer.go). It uses a service credential and has no subscription awareness, so it would send a Terra run's transcript to a paid Anthropic model.
- In the web app, Do equals `agentic` plus `plan_mode: true`. chat-client sends both from the same flag, so a Do run is read-only by construction: risky tools are refused, and effects need B's plan-approval wiring.
- The agent loop is seeded only with `goal`, with no thread history, persona or org instructions (agent.rs run_rounds L959-972).
- Final answers travel inside the JSON envelope with `max_tokens` 4096 (agent.rs L259), so a very long answer would be cut and fail to parse.
- The browser_agent tool cannot run inside RunAgent: `execute_step_with_subagent` passes no browser grant (runtime_loop/mod.rs L396-448), and the planner LLM is off unless `QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM=1` and then defaults to `verevon-balance` (llm_planner.rs L65, L94).
- Scheduled runs use a service credential and no user identity (execution-core grpc.rs L242-261, `scheduled_inference_request` L487-520: model verevon-balance, 1024 tokens). Integration Core would refuse a personal subscription for that principal (codex_subscription.go L292).

tasks.title: Typed subscription failures, run-level refusal latch, and a content-free usage log
files: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/subscription_refusal.rs (new: read the trailers off a tonic Status)

apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs (RoundsOutcome::InferFailed L393-400, L1086-1102; LoopContext L341; finalize L4125; record_managed_agent_terminal_outcome L4080; run_delegated_child L2509)
tasks.approach: execution-core reads x-mp-provider-error (the five codes plus too_long), x-mp-retry-after-ms and x-mp-resets-at from the failed Infer status. This is a copy of model-gateway's subscription_failure.rs, pinned by a contract test, which is the repo's own pattern. InferFailed carries an optional typed refusal. A shared slot on LoopContext (Arc<Mutex<Option<Refusal>>>, inherited by children) latches the first usage_limit or reauth refusal, so sibling fan-out items and later rounds stop calling the route and the root finalizes at once. Any other subscription failure (including an untyped 403 scope mismatch or a mismatch guard) becomes subscription_route_unavailable. finalize records the terminal failure_code 'provider_unavailable' (a code in Session Core's fixed vocabulary, see model-gateway session_flow.rs L822-835) and, for a typed refusal, skips the generic graceful assistant message. The gateway's Failed arm then emits ChatEvent::subscription_error directly, without emit_subscription_failure, because that helper would re-terminalize a run execution-core already settled, and appends the Norwegian message from subscription_failure::message with append_assistant_message_authenticated so the thread is honest on reload. Add one content-free tracing::info! per round (run id, depth, input, output and cache token counts from InferResponse, stop_reason) so Terra quota burn is visible; never log content or arguments.
tasks.tests: Unit, execution-core: scripted MockInference returning Status::unavailable with trailers for each code gives the matching failure_code, no GRACEFUL reply appended, terminal failure_code provider_unavailable; a usage_limit in one fan-out child stops its siblings and the parent; an untyped failure maps to subscription_route_unavailable; trailer spellings pinned by a contract test against inference-core's constants. Unit and e2e, model-gateway: a RunAgentResponse with failure_code subscription_usage_limit and resets_at produces a subscription_error frame with retryable=false and the reset time; the thread gets the fixed message. Live: only a natural limit can show the real message, so the live proof records it if it occurs; the bogus-connection probe in A6 (P2) covers the untyped path for free.

tasks.title: Agentic stream: follow the run concurrently, drop the 25 s idle floor, route-aware deadline
files: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs (agentic_run_stream: event tail L8655-8682, dispatch wait L8688-8711, final Sse::new L9063)
tasks.approach: First confirm the defect in a live Do turn: compare the time of the final done frame with the time execution-core logs finalize. Then replace the sequential 'tail until 25 s silence, then wait 30 s' with one loop using tokio::select! over the orchestration event stream and the dispatch JoinHandle. Forward step events as they arrive, stop when the dispatch resolves, then drain any buffered events for a short fixed grace so the last step update precedes the answer chunks. Replace the two fixed timeouts with one wall-clock deadline from AGENTIC_RUN_DEADLINE_SECS: default 120 s for non-subscription turns, 270 s for a subscription turn (below the 300 s token lifetime). On expiry keep today's behaviour exactly: agent_dispatch_unavailable, retryable, run left alone (the run finishes server-side and the answer is in the thread on reload). Add axum Sse keep_alive (15 s comment frames) so a silent Terra round does not look dead to proxies; nginx already allows 3600 s and the BFF stream client has no overall timeout (apps/gateway/src/config.rs L148), so those need no change. Do not add resume buffering for the agentic path here.

Latency and quota: every round is a Codex process spawn through the broker, about 35 tool definitions are re-sent each round, tool proposals are capped at 16 per round, and Do runs record no usage anywhere. Token lifetime: delegated bearers default to 300 s. A3's 270 s deadline and A4's 240 s wall clock keep new rounds inside that, but a stack with PLANE_TOKEN_TTL_* overrides must be checked.

designs.workstream: C. Wide research that actually scales
designs.goal: Make a wide-research fan-out work end to end from /chat: the user starts it explicitly in Do mode, the run gets a real per-item budget (not 2 one-round items), the cards show up, survive a reload and carry each item's answer, the run cannot silently exceed its credentials, concurrency, or org policy, and the limits on the ChatGPT subscription route are stated in the product instead of discovered as failures. Honest ceiling: 24 items is the realistic Terra target; 100 stays a hard cap, not a promise.
designs.current_state:
Everything below is by source reading in C:/dev/CoresSystem; nothing was run. Note first: the wide-research code (execution-core subagent/research_fan_out.rs, ChatWideResearchPanel.tsx, the agent.rs, subagent/mod.rs, execution.proto and orchestration.proto changes) is UNCOMMITTED, and research_fan_out.rs and the panel are untracked; sse.rs, http_routes.rs, session-core grpc files, DashboardComposer.tsx, use-chat-controller.ts, ChatPage.tsx and auth-core token files also carry other sessions' uncommitted edits.

What happens through chat today:
1. The only RunAgentRequest builder (model-gateway sse.rs spawn_run_dispatch ~8356) sends max_rounds 4 and max_subagents 0 (:8380, :8424). A fan-out in round 1 sees a pool of 3 (agent.rs:1438), one round is held back for the parent (research_fan_out.rs:144-162), so 2 items get 1 round and the rest are refused. A 1-round child that calls a tool ends Exhausted (agent.rs:2600-2607). Net: no usable item answer.
2. The budget design cannot scale even if the request fields are raised: the pool comes from the parent's own max_rounds, capped at MAX_ROUNDS_CEILING 32 (agent.rs:274), and delegated rounds are charged back to the parent loop (agent.rs:1551-1553, loop condition :1020). 100 items need about 200+ rounds.
3. Child-run registration answer ('could not register the delegated child run'): session-core refuses StartManagedRun without a user-bound credential (session-core/src/grpc.rs:6125-6127, PermissionDenied). Execution-core registers with its org-scoped service token (agent.rs:2106-2147; token provider session_terminal_auth.rs mints a service JWT with scope session:terminalize only, auth-core issues principal_type service with no user_id). RecordRunOutput needs session:write (grpc.rs:6214), which execution-core's session-core scopes lack (plane-service-principals.json:155-159). The unit-test fake accepts the service token (agent.rs:5443-5452). Effect: the fan-out still runs and returns its digest, but no child runs, lineage edges, attach/stop events (so no cards) and no durable child answers are written. AttachSubagent, RecordOrchestrationEvent and AppendMessage use the run's user bearer and are fine while it is valid.
4. Credential lifetime is the real wall: every delegated bearer (inference, session, data-plane, execution) is minted fresh at request start with a 300 s default TTL (convex-token.service.ts, no override in compose) and inference-core and session-core verify exp. Execution-core's finalize appends the assistant answer with the user session bearer (agent.rs:4148-4171) and falls back to a graceful failure reply if that fails. A run longer than about 5 minutes therefore loses its answer after spending its whole budget. On Terra at 60-120 s per item (assumption; the only data on record is per-turn follow-up p50 26.7 s / p95 41.6 s), 4-wide covers only about 6-8 items inside 300 s.
5. The chat stream gives up early: agentic_run_stream tails events with a 25 s idle timeout and then waits 30 s for RunAgent (sse.rs ~8672, ~8689). The live tail never ends on its own, so every Do turn idles 25 s after its last event, and a wide run with a quiet gap gets agent_dispatch_unavailable while it keeps running.
6. Panel: ChatWideResearchPanel subscribes with no cursor, and session-core's empty cursor means live tail only (orchestration_grpc.rs:3194). The replay ring is 256 events per run (:43), smaller than a big fan-out. LineageEdge has no goal, batch or child status (proto :426-438; fetch_lineage_for_thread selects metadata but the final SELECT drops it, :1547). After a reload the panel is empty.
7. Policy and cost: model-gateway already reads org-core quotas at admission (org_quota.rs, sse.rs:848, fails open) and org-core stores any key, so execution-core does not need an org-core client. No key for subagents exists and the BFF settable-key allowlist (apps/gateway domains/orgs/quotas.rs:27) has two entries. cost-core counts subscription-basis usage as 0 tokens and 0 USD (ledger.go:191-221), so there is no price guard on Terra; only breadth, rounds, wall clock and concurrency bound it. The existing per-call semaphore (default 4) is per fan-out call, not per run or org.
8. Route: Do is disabled for subscription models (DashboardComposer.tsx:1268, chat-client.ts:1029, normalize.rs:190-205) and the composer's Do toggle is plan_mode, which refuses risky tools but exempts subagent.* (agent.rs:1385-1387), so wide research is compatible with it. Execution-core infers with an empty subscription_connection_id (agent.rs:1070-1072) and compose defaults EXECUTION_AGENT_MODEL to model-router (deploy/docker-compose.yml:938), which silently overrides the requested model with the paid router. The ChatGPT broker allows 4 concurrent calls per connection with a 30 s queue (integration-corev2 internal/codexsubscription/limiter.go:11-12), so a 4-wide fan-out occupies the user's whole connection.

tasks.approach: A fan-out draws on its own run-level child round budget instead of the parent's remaining rounds. Resolution: per-child rounds default 4 (cap 6; a research item is search, read, answer), total default ceiling x per-child capped at 400, all clamped by deployment env and, via C5, by the org. Each item reserves min(per-child cap, even share of the budget) when it gets its permit and refunds unused rounds when it ends, which keeps the 2026-09-28 'divide evenly' ruling but moves it from the parent's pool to the child budget. The fan-out charges the parent 0 rounds, so the parent's max_rounds (chat sends 4; C5 raises wide turns to 6) is only for decomposing and synthesising, and total inference calls are bounded by parent rounds plus child budget. Ad hoc subagent.task keeps today's pool semantics. Also: on the last allowed round of a depth>0 loop send no tools, so an item that runs out of budget returns a partial answer instead of Exhausted. Report child_rounds_used and children_started in RunAgentResponse (feeds receipts and any live credit meter).

owner_decisions.question: D1. Budget semantics: keep the shared pool taken from the parent's rounds (2026-09-28 ruling, 'divide evenly'), or give a fan-out its own child round budget that is still divided evenly?
owner_decisions.options: (a) keep the pool and raise the round ceiling for fan-out only; (b) separate child budget, even division kept, parent charged 0; (c) leave as is (2 one-round items from chat)
owner_decisions.recommended: (b). It keeps the fairness the ruling wanted, but the pool cannot reach even 24 items under the 32-round ceiling, and charging children to the parent makes it end Exhausted before it can read the digest.

owner_decisions.question: D2. Default numbers for wide turns
owner_decisions.options: Wide ceiling 24 (hard cap 100); rounds per item 4 (cap 6); total child rounds at most 400; wall clock 900 s; fan-out concurrency 3 on the subscription route and 4 on metered routes; breaker after 3 provider failures; parent max_rounds 6 on wide turns
owner_decisions.recommended: Take these as env-tunable defaults and replace them with measured p50 item time and the observed broker queue behaviour after the C10 run. 100 items is a ceiling, not a Terra target: at 3-wide and about 90 s per item it takes roughly 50 minutes, longer than the 15-minute managed-run deadline. Detached, service-owned wide research would be a separate design.

owner_decisions.question: D3. Allow longer-lived (up to 1500 s) delegated bearers for wide-research turns only?
owner_decisions.options: (a) yes, scoped as in C9; (b) no, accept a hard limit of about 6-8 items on Terra within 300 s
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) after a short security review. Without it, 'scales' is not true on a slow route, and a run past 5 minutes loses its answer.

owner_decisions.question: D4. Entry point and gate

designs.live_proof:
Rule: Terra only (gpt-5.6-terra via openai-codex-subscription); never Verevon Balance or a paid provider. Today nothing about wide research can be proven live, because Do mode is off on that route and execution-core would route to model-router anyway; A (Do on the subscription route, letter assumed) is the prerequisite for steps 2 to 5.

Step 1, no Do mode needed, can run now (C1): one plain Terra chat turn to get a real thread and run id; a probe issues StartManagedRun, RecordRunOutput, AttachSubagent and RecordTerminalOutcome against the running session-core with the execution-core service token and with a user bearer, printing only gRPC codes. Expected today: service token refused on start and on record_run_output. After C1 the user-bearer path must succeed. This answers the 'could not register the delegated child run' question without a model call.

Step 2, after A, C1, C3, C5, C6, C7: Terra, Do on, 'Bred forskning' on, 6 items (one turn, about 30 subscription calls). Pass criteria: the effective model in the execution-core log is the Terra model, not the router; no 'could not register the delegated child run' warning; the lineage endpoint returns 6 edges with batch id, goal summary and completed child status; the panel shows 6 cards live and the same 6 after a reload mid-run and after completion (browser pane, wait 7 s after navigate, use computed-style or DOM probes); each card expands to the item's answer; RunAgentResponse child_rounds_used is within the budget; no broker_queue rate limit at concurrency 3; the final answer names every item with a status, and no item is Exhausted by a 1-round budget.

Step 3: C2 pass criteria on the same run: no agent_dispatch_unavailable, the answer arrives within a few seconds of the last event.

Step 4, only if step 2 passed and Terra allowance remains: 12 items to measure p50 item time and total wall clock; record them, and use them to set D2 defaults. A run that crosses 300 s passes only with C9 deployed; without C9, the pass criterion is a clean early stop with the stated reason, not a lost answer.

Step 5: set max_subagents_per_run=3 on the test org through the admin quota API and confirm a 6-item request runs 3 and refuses 3 with the org reason.

Cannot be proven live: the subscription usage-limit breaker (would require exhausting the cap), 100 items (cost, time and the 15-minute managed deadline), and any ZDR behaviour. Those stay on mocked tests and are labelled so in the evidence record. Until the Terra cap reset (project memory: 2026-10-03 17:45 UTC) steps 2 to 5 should not be attempted.

designs.current_state:
Read by code, not run. Aliases used below: FE = apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3, MP = apps/Model Plane. Letters other than H were not given to me, so other dependencies are named by capability.

Corrections and new findings beyond the audit text:
1. Resume across restart: the Redis backend exists (MP model-gateway stream_buffer.rs:404 from_env) but the model-gateway compose block (MP/deploy/docker-compose.yml from line 191) sets no REDIS_URL, and http_routes.rs:72 is a bare `axum::serve(listener, app).await` with no graceful drain, so SIGTERM kills every in-flight turn. After a restart the SPA's followUnresumableRun (use-chat-controller.ts:1408) polls the run until session-core terminalises it, up to 15 minutes (terminalization.rs MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS). Redis alone only replays frames already sent; nothing finishes the stream.
2. Citations: the server already emits `number` on every citation frame (sse_events.rs payload) and anchors by it, but the client drops it (chat-client.ts emitCitation :906, normalizeCitation :1297) and binds [n] to citations[n-1] (chat-media-markdown.tsx parseInline). Each web_search call restarts numbering at 1 (tool_loop.rs web_search_citations ~5644).
3. Skills: auto-matched skills inject on every route (sse.rs:1506-1560 fetch_skill_context is route-agnostic). Only explicit slash picks are dropped on Terra, by the SPA (chat-client.ts ~:1049, DashboardComposer commandNeedsFullRoute :558). normalize.rs:190-205 does not reject skill_ids. The audit row 'skills are off on Terra' is half wrong.
4. Branch: branchAt (use-chat-controller.ts:3745) copies turns client-side only; the model's context for the branch starts empty while the screen shows the history. This is a silent wrong behaviour, not just a missing feature.
5. Regenerate and edit: the server appends the user text again (session_flow.rs prepare_managed_run_with_bearer ~:470) and keeps the discarded answer. Editing an earlier turn truncates only the screen; later turns stay in the model's history (ListConversation, sse.rs ~:4968). 'Fortsett' sends the whole continuation instruction plus the partial answer as the user message (use-chat-controller.ts:2532, buildContinuationModelContent :211), which is persisted and never stripped on reload.
6. Idempotency guard (sse.rs:931-960) is dormant: nothing in the SPA sets idempotency_key, and the SPA has no handler for duplicate_in_flight. The BFF passes unknown body fields through (shared::normalized_model_body).
7. Reasoning: the Terra path emits no reasoning text anywhere. Three hops are empty: appserver.go reads only item/agentMessage/delta (:996), codex_subscription.rs sets reasoning_delta to '' (:444, :482, :508), and the broker stream event has no reasoning type. The downstream half (ReasoningDelta, derive.ts node, popover) exists. Whether Codex emits summaries for gpt-5.6-terra is unknown and needs a spike.
8. Search: the sidebar search is a client substring over title, preview and project name (chat-organization.ts selectOrganizedChats). No index exists; recall_memory (tool_loop.rs:3151) is the model for a recall_conversations tool.
9. OCR: the extractor (Ingestion Plane imports-core app/chat_extract.py) is deliberately local-only with a 1 MB cap (also prepare-chat-attachments.ts:19); a scanned PDF returns 422. Most multi-page scans exceed 1 MB before OCR could matter.
10. Usage: the usage event is emitted once per turn (sse.rs:3853, :6589). On Terra there is no price. The broker already parses account/rateLimits snapshots (integration-corev2 appserver.go:1065, :288) but uses them only on failure.
11. Spaces: the BFF creates only personal and room Spaces (spaces.rs ~2866); a Space thread has origin='space' and never appears in the chat sidebar (origin=chat filter, migration 0034). Chat 'projects' are per-browser localStorage folders.
12. Learning loop: the reviewer calls inference-core with no subscription connection (capability-core cmd/main.go:760, llmreviewer/reviewer.go:126), so it runs on the default paid route and cannot run on Terra.
13. The project notes say the Codex usage limit resets 2026-10-03 17:45 UTC; schedule live proofs after that.

tasks.approach: Two independent fixes. (a) Drain: today SIGTERM drops every producer, so any launcher redeploy kills turns in flight. With graceful shutdown the old container finishes its streams (they already detach from a disconnected client), then exits; compose waits up to the grace period. (b) Set REDIS_URL so frames already sent survive a hard crash. Dragonfly is already in compose (cache_mode, 256 MB, shared with capability-core and sandbox-manager), keys are 10-minute TTL and capped at 4096 frames. All of this is from reading the code; nothing was run.

EXPORT: chat-export (src/features/chat/lib/chat-export/) is pure TypeScript: docx.ts, xlsx.ts, pptx.ts, a store-only zip.ts, ooxml.ts. PDF is not a file. print.ts clones the rendered DOM into a hidden iframe and calls win.print(), so the user must use the browser's Save-as-PDF dialog. Call sites: ChatMessages.tsx runExport (L547) and exportMenuItems (L593), and ChatArtifactPanel.tsx runExport. print.ts has no tests. Exports carry no charts. A Mermaid block exports as code text.

CHARTS: there is no chart library. Tables render through MarkdownTable (ChatMessages.tsx L1405) with no copy, CSV or chart control. MarkdownCodeBlock (L1134) turns a closed mermaid fence into a diagram. HTML artifacts run in a sandboxed iframe with no network (shared/lib/sandbox-html.ts), so only hand-written SVG works. No server text steers the model toward Mermaid or any chart form.

UPLOAD EXTRACTION: imports-core app/parsers.py reads xlsx cell values only from cached <v> (_xlsx_cell_text L160), so formulas without a cached value read as empty. It has no styles.xml handling, so date cells arrive as serial numbers. Booleans and errors are not handled. Merged and hidden sheets are not labelled. pptx (_pptx_slide_text L230) skips speaker notes, tables lose their row structure, and charts and alt text are skipped. There is no zip-size guard, so a 1 MB zip bomb is read unbounded. Over-length text gives 413 (chat_extract.py), where a truncation with a marker would be friendlier. Tests use hand-built zips only (tests/test_chat_extract.py), never a file authored in real Excel or PowerPoint. Caps are 1 MB, 60k characters per file and 120k per turn (prepare-chat-attachments.ts L18-35). The BFF body limit is axum's default 2 MB.

SANDBOX AND code_interpreter, which matters for the live-proof rule: the audit says Plan mode, wide research and connector tools need Do mode. code_interpreter does not. By reading, the in-chat tool loop runs on the subscription route (sse.rs L2154 subscription_tool_round; tool_loop.rs L6640-6750 decide tool calls through the broker). The gateway always adds builtin_tool_defs(), which includes code_interpreter, unless the web search gate removes web_search (sse.rs L1644). conversation_tool_allowed also allows it (tool_loop.rs L4215). normalize.rs L190-205 only rejects req.tools, attachments, agentic and plan_mode, so the tools feature passes. So code_interpreter should be callable on Terra today. That is unproven live: every record is Verevon Balance, and the audit found no docx, pdf, pptx or chart ever produced live. The sandbox image has numpy, pandas, matplotlib, openpyxl, xlsxwriter, python-docx, reportlab, pypdf, PIL, lxml and python-pptx 1.0.2 (execution-core/Dockerfile L59-82). The model-visible description (tool_loop.rs L4306-4309) omits python-pptx, xlsxwriter, pypdf and PIL. The health probe only runs python3 --version (health_attest.rs interpreter_available, ~L222). Input files reach the sandbox only as base64 the model types itself: files_in is built by hand, and uploaded binaries never leave the browser (and attachments are rejected on Terra). The gateway already parses the '--- VEDLEGG: name ---' blocks of attached text (source_validation.rs SourceContext::from_messages L22-84, document_contract.rs L92), so it can stage the extracted text without any new transport.

CODE UI: a code_interpreter call renders as a read-only collapsible ToolCallCard (ChatMessages.tsx L1959). GeneratedFiles (L2684) and GeneratedImagePreviews (L2623) already deliver files, with no test for GeneratedFiles. The artifact panel shows code with line numbers and no run control. execution-core ExecuteStep is unary and checks run ownership with authorize_durable_run_owner (grpc.rs L797-830). There is no streaming execution, so Code mode (tools callable from the sandbox) needs new infrastructure.

LSP: lsp.rs is a pass-through to an external bridge that is only in the opt-in overlay docker-compose.bridges.yml, with no consumer anywhere.

OCR: model-gateway has /v1/ai/documents/layout and /v1/ai/images/ocr backed by Azure Document Intelligence (inference-core provider/doc_intel.rs, needs AZURE_DOCUMENT_INTELLIGENCE_ENDPOINT and KEY). imports-core refuses an image-only PDF with 422 and uses a slim Python image with no OCR engine.

tasks.approach: xlsx: (1) _xlsx_styles(zf) reads xl/styles.xml cellXfs and numFmts into a per-style kind: date, datetime, time, percent or general. Built-in date ids are 14-22, 27-36, 45-47 and 50-58. For a custom code, strip quoted literals, backslash escapes, [color] and elapsed brackets, then it is a date if any of y m d h s remain. Percent means a % in the code, with decimals counted. Read workbookPr date1904 from workbook.xml. (2) _xlsx_cell_text gets the style map: t=b gives TRUE/FALSE; t=e keeps the error text; a cell with <f> and no <v> gives '=' plus the formula text (an empty shared-formula child gives '=(delt formel)'); a date-styled number is converted from the serial (epoch 1899-12-30, with the 1900 leap-day quirk for serials under 61; 1904 system if flagged) to ISO YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM; a percent-styled number is shown as a percentage; other numbers are normalised to 15 significant digits so 0.30000000000000004 does not reach the model. (3) _xlsx_sheet_parts also returns state, and hidden sheets print as '[Name] (skjult)'. Keep the existing '[Name]' header and tab-separated rows, because the current tests assert that exact shape. (4) After the grid, one '[Formler]' section lists up to 100 'Sheet!B10: =SUM(B2:B9)' lines. (5) Stream worksheets with ET.iterparse and clear(), and stop at about 55,000 characters with '[… avkortet: N rader utelatt i «Ark»]', returning truncated:true. Today the same workbook is refused with 413. pptx: (6) _pptx_slide_text walks spTree in order. Table cells become tab-separated rows per a:tr. A picture's cNvPr descr becomes '[Bilde: …]'. The title placeholder text goes first. A chart reached through the slide rels (type .../chart) becomes '[Diagram: tittel] serie: verdier; kategorier: …' from the cached c:v values. (7) _pptx_notes_text follows the slide rels to the notesSlide and takes only the body placeholder text, giving a '[Notater]' block. A slide with show="0" is labelled '(skjult)'. A slide without notes keeps the output '[Slide 1]\nTitle' that the current test asserts. Both: (8) _zip_budget() checks total ZipInfo.file_size (cap 30 MB), member count (cap 2000) and single-part size before any read, so a 1 MB zip bomb ends in 413 without allocating. Keep Python's default expat entity protections. Do not raise the 1 MB attachment cap here (see owner decision on caps).

tasks.approach: Spec: the model writes a closed fence ```chart with JSON {type: bar|line|area|pie, title, x|categories, series:[{name, values}], unit, stacked}. Limits: 24 categories, 6 series (pie: 1 series, 8 slices), finite numbers (numeric strings pass through detectExcelNumber). A bad spec never throws: the block falls back to the normal code block with a one-line note. An unclosed fence stays a code block while streaming, exactly like mermaid at L1137, so the chart appears when the fence closes. Table-to-chart: chartFromTable takes the first non-numeric column as categories and every numeric column as a series; it parses Norwegian numbers ('1 234,5', '12 %', '3,2 MNOK') through detectExcelNumber and strips unit suffixes; it picks line for date-like categories and bar otherwise, with a bar, line and pie switch in the UI. It returns null when there is no numeric column, so the toolbar shows no chart button. Renderer: one SVG per chart, tokens from global.css with a dark-theme pair; load the dataviz skill for the palette and contrast; series are told apart by legend marker and order, not colour alone; role=img with title and desc; focusable marks with aria-labels and tooltips; always include a visually hidden data table; an SVG download button. tasks.approach: Smallest design, and only after a spike. The sandbox has no network, but a Unix socket file inside the writable workspace (bind-mounted) is reachable across the network namespace. execution-core listens on <workspace>/.rpc.sock for the length of one run; a staged verevon_tools.call(tool, **args) writes one JSON request and reads one JSON response. execution-core answers each request by calling the same executor the normal ExecuteStep path uses, with the bearers it already authenticated for that call (data-plane, inference, session), so the policy, hook and permission gates stay at the boundary exactly as for any tool. An allowlist admits only tools marked read-only (knowledge_search first; the tools that need an ingestion or browser bearer are not reachable from ExecuteStep and stay out). Each call has a result cap, a call-count cap (50) and the existing wall-clock limit (raise to 60 s for code mode only), and every call is recorded in the step output as {tool, args_digest, status, bytes} so the receipt shows what the program did. Intermediate results never enter model context, which is the point. Effectful tools are out of scope and wait for the owner. First step is a half-day spike on Linux to prove the bwrap socket path (bwrap bind plus AF_UNIX connect under --unshare-net); if it fails, the fallback is a stdio protocol that needs a streaming ExecuteStep, which is a proto change and a bigger project.

owner_decisions.question: OCR engine for scanned PDFs (and optionally images on the Terra route)?

owner_decisions.question: May end users run their own edited code in the hermetic sandbox (the editable cell, H7)?

tasks.approach: Split read from write at the tool boundary, the same way list/read_subagent_result are split. (1) New tool read_provider_action {connection_id, operation, params}. It hard-refuses anything where operation_is_write(op) != Some(false) with a message pointing to execute_provider_action. It resolves the token exactly like read_action_json (delegated exchange per call), sends no approvalId and no attestation, and is bound in trusted_capability_id to the existing LOW capability cap.tool.provider.read, so it is not caught by the name-only HIGH 'ask' on cap.tool.provider.execute. Verify that cap.tool.provider.read already sits in agent.rs's UNATTESTED_BASELINE (l.~3300) like its sibling list_provider_actions; if the capability-tool contract test objects, record the new tool next to it. Its name contains none of the is_risky_tool keywords, so plan mode and the ReadOnly rung allow it. Do not add it to ACTION_TOOL_NAMES. (2) Catalog: add mail.messages.get, gmail.messages.get, drive.file.content, sharepoint.sites, sharepoint.drives as is_write:false; rewrite the summaries to document the F2-F4 params compactly (shared params stated once at the top of the listing), each op tagged with the capability it needs (mail.read, gmail.read, calendar.read, sharepoint.read, drive.read). The listing marks an op on a connection whose capabilities lack it ('needs reconnect: calendar'), states that Microsoft and Google connections are personal and shown only to their owner, and says plainly when delegation fell back (today it silently says no connections exist). Keep each connection block under ~1.5k characters. (3) Results: replace the 2000-char JSON cut for reads with per-op renderers that produce compact text: mail row = id | date | from | subject | 140-char preview | attachments yes/no; event row = id | start-end local | title | location | attendee count; file row = id | name | type | size | modified; message and file bodies in a fixed delimiter block that content cannot forge. Hard budget 7,500 characters per result (under the loop's 8,000 cap in agent.rs l.279), dropping whole rows, never mid-record, and ending with a machine-usable footer: next: {pageToken} for lists, or next: {offset} for long bodies (maxChars param, default 6,000). Outlook ids are ~150 characters, so budget rows accordingly. (4) A kill switch PROVIDER_READ_TOOL_ENABLED, same pattern as research_fan_out::enabled(), default off in the image until D1 is answered. (5) Surgical edits only in agent.rs and mod.rs: other sessions have uncommitted work there; put all new logic in connector_reads.rs and touch the shared files at the five seams listed. No full-file writes.
tasks.tests: Unit: renderer table tests (UTF-8 boundaries, whole-row dropping, budget never exceeded, offset paging reassembles the body exactly, Outlook-length ids); operation_is_write asserts for every new op and its microsoft./google. alias; read_provider_action refuses mail.send, gmail.send, pages.post and an unknown op; trusted_capability_id maps the new tool; offered_tool_defs invariants (unique names, capability binding); permission rung test for the new tool; listing under 7,500 characters for a Microsoft plus Google plus Meta org. Integration (wiremock, as integration_tools.rs already does): auth-core exchange 200 then integration-corev2 fixtures built from F2-F4 shapes; exchange 403 path states the fallback; 401 does not fall back; postcondition read-back for gmail.send unchanged. A RunAgent loop test with a scripted model calling list then read. Live: needs a Do run (A); see F13.

tasks.approach: drive.file.content returns base64 (<=1 MB), which is useless to a model. Slice 1, no new authority: text-like files are decoded in Rust, Google-native files use F4's exportAs=text, and an Office or PDF file returns an honest 'needs extraction' message that points to the composer picker. Slice 2, behind D6: execution-core mints an ingestion token with the narrow scope imports:extract (never imports:write, which can create import jobs) and posts the bytes to imports-core /api/v1/import/extract, the same extractor the picker uses, so limits and behaviour stay identical. imports-core needs two small changes: accept imports:extract for that one path, and an optional max_chars so a long document is returned up to 400,000 characters instead of the current dead-end 413 at 60,000; the default is unchanged for the BFF. execution-core pages the extracted text (offset and maxChars, 6,000 per call) and caches it briefly so paging does not re-download. Source cap stays a hard reject with the byte counts in the message; never silently truncate (connector-picker spec rule 4). A scanned PDF with no text returns imports-core's 422 text, surfaced as-is.
tasks.tests: imports-core: pytest for max_chars bounds, default unchanged, imports:extract accepted only on the extract path, imports:write still required elsewhere. Rust: wiremock for imports-core 200, 413, 415, 422; paging reassembles; cache hit does not re-download; over-cap error text. Policy: auth-core policy contract spec still passes with the new scope. Live: slice 1 on Terra via the picker is not applicable; slice 2 needs a Do run (A).
