owner_decisions.question: D1. May the agent read the run owner's own mail, files and calendar without a per-call approval?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Autonomous reads through read_provider_action (LOW capability), only of the run owner's own connections, with untrusted-content framing, durable redaction and an org kill switch; writes stay human-approved and attested. (b) One consent per run before the first personal-data read. (c) Per-call approval (what the HIGH capability gives by accident today, and unusable).
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). Ship F6 behind PROVIDER_READ_TOOL_ENABLED, default off, and turn it on once the owner says yes. The 2026-09-28 critic's 'no tool becomes agent-autonomous' default was an interim position; the owner-only ruling plus delegated identity now bound the data to the run's own user.

owner_decisions.question: D2. Where should the agent read connected data: Do mode only, or also plain Ask mode through model-gateway tools (F12)?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Do mode only, relying on A to make Do runs testable on the Terra route. (b) Also Ask mode now (F12): works on Terra today and is the natural place to answer 'what did X write', but adds tool schemas to every Terra turn and a second client.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) for now. Revisit when A reports whether Do can run on the subscription route; if it cannot, take F12 (guarded by a per-thread connectors switch) because it is then the only live proof and the only way the owner's own route can use this.

owner_decisions.question: D3. Should mail from a personal Microsoft or Google connection appear in the org-wide shared inbox?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Keep org-wide for every connection (contradicts the 2026-09-28 owner-only ruling). (b) Add connection visibility personal or org; only org-visibility connections feed the shared inbox and skip the owner check. (c) Tag synced conversations with their owner and filter the read lane.
owner_decisions.recommended: (b), with an explicit 'share this mailbox with the organization' choice at connect time, and existing inbox connections switched to org only on the owner's say-so. Until then, state that inbox_search is org-wide.

owner_decisions.question: D4. How is Calendars.Read granted for Microsoft?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Connect path only: a 'calendar' source and bundle in Settings and the picker prompt. (b) Also add Calendars.Read to the sign-in scopes so every Microsoft login grants it.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). (b) changes the consent prompt at every login and the sign-in handoff would then widen every connection.

owner_decisions.question: D5. Should personal-data reads be allowed in ZDR or temporary chats?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Refuse (fail closed, like the picker's temporary-chat block). (b) Allow, with the model route's ZDR guarantees.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). The Terra route already rejects ZDR, so this costs nothing there.

owner_decisions.question: D6. Give execution-core a narrow imports:extract scope so the agent can read Office files and PDFs?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Yes: new scope imports:extract on POST /api/v1/import/extract only, added to model-execution's ingestion scopes. (b) No: text-only first slice (text files and Google-native exports), Office and PDF stay picker-only. (c) Do extraction inside integration-corev2 with its own principal (same policy change, different principal).
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), with slice 1 of F7 shipping first so F6 is not blocked. Never grant imports:write to the agent's service principal.

owner_decisions.question: D7. Add SharePoint site and library browsing to the composer picker now?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Not now: the agent reads SharePoint through F4 and F6 first. (b) Add a SharePoint tab to the picker in this workstream.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). It matches the 2026-09-28 ruling (OneDrive personal and My Drive only); pick up (b) later, reusing the SharePointLibraryPicker shapes.

owner_decisions.question: D8. Which accounts and tenant are used for live proof?
owner_decisions.options: (a) A dedicated Microsoft 365 developer or sandbox tenant with a SharePoint site and admin consent for Sites.Read.All, plus a dedicated Gmail account, seeded with fixed fixtures. (b) The owner's production mailboxes.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), connected by the owner (OAuth consent is an owner action). Never production mailboxes.

owner_decisions.question: D9. Before enabling reads for customer orgs, require approval for egress tools after a run has read content that screened as injected (F8b)?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Yes: after a Flagged read, web_fetch, web_search, browser_agent and writes need approval for the rest of the run. (b) No: framing note only, like web results today.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) before any customer org uses it; (b) is acceptable for internal Terra testing. Note that requires_read_only has no caller today, so this is new enforcement, not a flag flip.

risks: Unverified Graph behaviour is baked into F2 and F3: whether $search can be combined with $filter or $orderby on messages, that events do not support $search, whether the Prefer timezone header takes IANA names, the InefficientFilter rule. I could not run anything. Capture real responses during F10 and turn them into test fixtures; do not trust the plan's assumptions over a live response.

Finding 3 (name-only capability gate, HIGH 'ask' for every execute_provider_action) is from reading code, not observed. If capability-core answers differently live, F6's separate read tool is still correct but the urgency changes. F13 settles it. The new tool reuses cap.tool.provider.read, which sits in the unattested-capability quarantine (ledger.md l.1547); availability of that capability is also unproven live.

Prompt injection and exfiltration: mail and files carry attacker text, the Do agent also has web_fetch and web_search, and writes are the only gated egress. F8 adds scanning and framing, but enforcement of Flagged content is not built (D9). Do not enable F6 for customer orgs before D9 is answered.

Privacy: mail text must not reach the durable session-core step record (F8 redaction) or logs; integration-corev2's audit event records only the operation name, so add connection id and result count (never content) if the owner wants a usable trail.

Collisions with other sessions' uncommitted work: execution-core agent.rs and mod.rs, model-gateway tool_loop.rs and verevon_actions.rs, DashboardComposer.tsx, plane-service-principals.json and run-control-plane.sh. Use new modules and surgical Edit calls, never full-file writes, never revert, stash or commit. The frontend container serves live source: check git status before any restart. Build only through the launcher (Go via the ingestion stage, Rust via the model-plane-only copy with LAST_STACK_INDEX=2, BFF via the frontend stage). Use Write/Edit for code containing backslashes and check CRLF with node, not grep.

Reconnect semantics: persistConnection replaces capabilities today; F5 changes it to a union. Review that no flow depends on narrowing by reconnecting, and keep the Meta branch (which verifies scopes) untouched.

Business tenants: default Entra policy blocks user self-consent to Sites.Read.All, which the default connect already requests, and Verevon has no publisher verification or admin-consent flow (another workstream). SharePoint live proof needs a tenant where it is consented; a non-admin user in a default tenant may not be able to connect at all.

The exchanged-token single-use cache in integration-corev2 is process-local (known limit). A delegated child run's session bearer is untested. Delegation falls back silently on 403; F6 makes the fallback visible in tool output, but the log line must also stay at warn.

Tokens and size: Outlook ids are ~150 characters, so a 25-row page costs most of the 7,500-character budget; the F6 budget drops rows and gives a pageToken. Gmail headers cost one API call per message (5 quota units each); cap and concurrency are bounded, and the BFF rate limiter must tolerate debounced picker typing.

Live-proof ceiling: nothing in execution-core, the token exchange or agent tool selection can be shown live without A or F12. Google paths cannot be shown without a Gmail test account; SharePoint without a consented tenant. F10 proves the provider-facing half only.

The code comment and the audit cite docs/actions-surface-operations.md as the authoritative operations list, but that file does not exist under integration-corev2/docs; create it or fix the references when the new ops land, or the catalog and the executor will drift again.
designs.live_proof: Rule: every live run uses gpt-5.6-terra via openai-codex-subscription, never Verevon Balance or a paid provider, never prints a token or bearer, and uses dedicated test accounts (D8) that the owner connects. STAGE 0, no model, no Do mode (F1): from inside the execution-core container, post a deliberately invalid subject token to auth-core's token-exchange endpoint. 400 or 401 means the delegation grant is active; 403 means execution-core would silently fall back and the owner must run the Control-plane launcher stage. STAGE 1, provable now on Terra without Do mode (F10, after F2-F5 and F9 are built through the launcher): the composer picker 'Fra en tilkoblet kilde' reads through the BFF and integration-corev2 with the user's own bearer and inlines text, so Terra can read it. Assertions: Outlook and Gmail search finds the seeded token; Gmail rows show subject and sender; the picked mail's seeded phrase appears in Terra's answer; the OneDrive folder pages without duplicates; docx and xlsx text (including a formula's cached value) reaches Terra; a file over 1 MB is refused with the size message; the Outlook event shows 09:00 local after the owner's one-time calendar reconnect and the specific capability message before it; SharePoint sites, libraries and a driveId read work through BFF probes; a second user is refused with personal_connection_forbidden; integration-corev2 logs one audit event per read and no bearer value. This proves the provider ops, BFF, imports-core extraction and Terra reading. It does not exercise delegation, execution-core, the catalog, the capability gate or the agent's tool choice. STAGE 2, needs a Do run that is allowed for testing (workstream A, or F12 if the owner takes it): F13's eight checks, namely the personal connections appear in list_provider_actions through a 200 token exchange, read_provider_action returns the seeded mail, file, event and site, the run never pauses for approval on a read, step records hold no content, no DELEGATION_NOT_CONFIGURED fallback in the log, and a second user sees nothing; also whether a delegated child run can read. Cannot be proven live until A: everything in execution-core (F6, F7 slice 2, F8 behaviour), the capability-gate finding, delegated-identity reads, injection framing in a real run, and the model's tool-selection quality. Cannot be proven live without extra accounts: Google (needs a Gmail test account) and SharePoint on a business tenant (needs Sites.Read.All consent). Record each stage in a dated evidence note under apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/product-recordings/evidence/ with screenshots and secret-free network captures.

designs.workstream: D. Scheduled runs that do real work and deliver a result; background notifications
designs.goal: A schedule made from chat fires on time, runs a bounded draft-only agent (v1: web research) as the owner on the owner's own route (including the ChatGPT Terra subscription), writes the result into a thread the owner can open, notifies them (bell plus deep link), and 'Se resultater' opens it. Plain chat turns get a 'Varsle meg' control so a long turn can finish in the background with a notice.
designs.current_state:
Verified by reading code on 2026-10-01 (nothing run).

Create and manage works: ScheduleDialog, /schedule, reply-menu 'Planlegg dette', ScheduledRunsPanel, BFF relaxation for own personal-Space schedules (agent_actions.rs authorize_own_schedule :533), user-core Phase B own-scheduled-thread read decision (committed; spaces.go issueThreadReadDecision :640 falls back to ResolveOwnScheduledThreadReadDecisionEvidence), BFF transcript route GET /api/v1/spaces/{ref}/threads/{id}/transcript (spaces.rs :2605).

What a fire does today: capability-core sweeper.fireOne (sweeper.go :226) makes a task and a cron_fires row ('pending') -> workflow_dispatcher.Dispatch -> PrepareScheduledRunThread (service-owned thread, owner service:orchestrator-core) -> ScheduledRunSupervision -> executeScheduledStepLoop -> ExecuteScheduledStepActivity -> execution-core execute_scheduled_step_runtime (grpc.rs :238): ONE inference on 'verevon-balance', max_tokens 1024, tool_choice none, system line 'Do not call tools'. Only a sha256 of the output is stored (receipt). The text returns to Go inside the activity result (so it lands in Temporal history) and nothing writes it to the thread. The thread therefore has zero messages.

Gaps found beyond the audit:
(1) The lane cannot start on any current policy: plane-service-principals.json gives orchestrator-core no execution-core audience / model:schedule:step, execution-core no inference-core audience and no session:scheduled-step; the Control credentials in compose are empty-default; release register says fail-closed; no fire has ever been recorded.
(2) cron_fires.status is never advanced after insert (only 'pending' or 'failed' at insert; the only UPDATE cron_fires in the repo is gdpr.rs :409). tasks.status is the real state (closed by taskexec RunCompletionConsumer.closeTask or Executor.failTask).
(3) orchestrator never terminalizes the run row in session-core (CompleteRunActivity/FailRunActivity only publish NATS), so a scheduled run shows as in flight forever in the Space Work tab.
(4) Run-watch exists end to end (BFF run_watchers.rs -> model-gateway -> capability-core runwatch -> notification-core) but only AgentRunConsole calls it. The chat live run panel (liveRunId, use-chat-controller.ts :415) only exists for plan or research turns, so it is unreachable on Terra. The reachable place is the waiting state (ThinkingDots, ChatMessages.tsx). Plain Terra turns do emit RUN_COMPLETED through managed terminalization (terminalization.rs :327), so a run watch on a plain turn should work and is live-provable on Terra.
(5) Delivered notifications link nowhere useful: notification-core stores cta_href (feed/types.go :42; mail_task_drafted.go :180 sets it) but gateway navbar.rs :172 only reads href|link|url, so the bell falls back to /inbox. Copy is generic ('Run <id> finished').
(6) Digest chain risk: the BFF digests serde_json::to_vec(template) (spaces.rs :515-520) while capability-core digests Go json.Marshal (workplane_apis.go :946-955), which escapes < > & as < etc. A goal containing '&' probably fails create with 403. Also task_template and config_json are JSONB, which reorders nested keys, so a nested object in the template would break the fire-time digest check (workflow_dispatcher.go :403, workflowreg.go :309). Needs a failing test first.
(7) list_cron (agent_actions.rs :421) returns every org schedule, including colleagues' goal text, to any member; the panel filters client-side only.
(8) System-owned threads/runs are readable by any org-authenticated session:read caller (session-core auth.rs authorize_owner_row :398, Read intent = org equality), so the own-thread decision is additive, not a gate.
(9) 'Se resultater' is a disabled button (ScheduledRunsPanel.tsx :135-142); /schedule is withheld on subscription routes (DashboardComposer.tsx commandNeedsFullRoute :558) because the lane only runs on Balance.
(10) The subscription route needs a user-bound inference identity (inference-core auth.rs budget_user_id :198; codex_subscription.rs request_body requires org, user and connection id). The lane deliberately uses an org-scoped service token (scheduled_inference_auth.rs). A schedule must not pin a connection id: model-selection.ts :127-165 says persisted ids are hints and reconnecting replaces them.

Design chosen (smallest end-to-end): keep the service-owned thread, Control decisions and receipts. Replace the single call with a small purpose-built read-only agent loop inside the scheduled step (not RunAgent, whose finalize terminalizes the run with a user bearer and whose session writes are refused for a system-owned run). Draft-only by construction: offered tools are an allowlist of read-only tools, so there is nothing to approve and a NeedsApproval step still fails the run. Session-core, not Temporal, persists the output into the thread. Results are read through the existing personal-Space decision path. Notification rides the existing run-watch consumer with context and a working link.

owner_decisions.question: 1. May a scheduled step act as the schedule owner on the subscription route (D10)? Without it a scheduled run can only use Verevon-managed models, so nothing in this workstream can be proven live under the Terra-only rule.
owner_decisions.options: (a) Decision-bound token exchange limited to inference-core, 120 s, subscription route only, adversarial review before activation. (b) inference-core verifies the Control decision itself. (c) No owner identity: scheduled runs on managed models only, unit-proven only.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), with the adversarial security review as a hard gate. Scheduled work then never borrows a human's bearer; it gets a one-step, decision-bound token.

owner_decisions.question: 2. Apply the policy and credential activation for the scheduled lane (D1)? It edits the service-principal policy (security configuration) and needs the launcher run from the Control plane.
owner_decisions.options: Apply now / apply after D4 is merged / do not activate.
owner_decisions.recommended: Prepare everything now; apply after you confirm in chat, in the same window as the D4 build, so the lane is never live in its old single-call form.

owner_decisions.question: 3. What may a scheduled run read in v1?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Web only. (b) Plus org-visible knowledge (matches how system runs already read). (c) Plus the owner's personal Outlook, Gmail and drive (needs a delegated read for service runs; conflicts with the owner-only ruling unless delegated).
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) for v1. Knowledge next, after D10's pattern is extended to the data plane. Connectors last.

owner_decisions.question: 4. Where does the owner see a result?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Read-only transcript from the personal Space (Phase B path) plus a 'Fortsett i chat' hand-off that seeds a new user-owned chat. (b) Deliver the result into a user-owned chat thread through PrepareUserOwnedThread, a new decision family and a new thread origin (M to L).
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) now. (b) only if people do not find or cannot act on the drawer.

owner_decisions.question: 5. Cadence floor, quotas and failure handling (D11).
owner_decisions.options: Floor 1 hour for non-admins, 10 active schedules per creator, auto-pause after 3 consecutive failures with a notice, 'Kjor na' once per 10 minutes, no automatic retry of a failed fire.
owner_decisions.recommended: Exactly that. It also keeps a capped ChatGPT subscription from being drained by retries.

owner_decisions.question: 6. Notification surface and content.
owner_decisions.options: (a) Bell plus unread count, title and link only, no content preview. (b) Add a short preview. (c) Also browser or OS push or email.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). The feed row persists in notification-core and preview text is customer content. Push and email only when asked, through notification preferences.

owner_decisions.question: 7. When the ChatGPT subscription is capped or disconnected at fire time.
owner_decisions.options: Fail visibly with the reason and notify (no fallback to Verevon Balance), versus fall back to a managed model.
owner_decisions.recommended: Fail visibly, no fallback. This matches your 2026-09-28 ruling of no failover on the subscription route.

owner_decisions.question: D1. Write approvals for calendar, Excel/Sheets and file saves: always ask, or trusted after N clean runs?
owner_decisions.options: (a) always ask every time, per write; (b) ask once per chat for reversible creates; (c) trusted after N clean runs per operation class; (d) never ask for own-calendar creates.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) for v1, for every write, including overwrite, delete and any cell edit. Risk classes recorded in the card: create-new (reversible), overwrite (shows before/after, eTag or hash guard), delete (extra confirm), outbound-notify (blocked in v1, see D4). Revisit (b) for create-new only after four weeks of receipts and read-back results; never auto for overwrite, delete or attendees.

owner_decisions.question: D2. Contacts: scope and compliance sign-off.
owner_decisions.options: (a) read-only lookup by name/email, no sync, no index, minimised fields, off until counsel signs; (b) full contact sync into knowledge; (c) do not build.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). Build G15 behind a flag, keep it disabled until counsel reviews it; do not add contacts to any default bundle. Counsel reviews are all still Pending in docs/compliance/README.md.

owner_decisions.question: D3. Business-tenant consent strategy.
owner_decisions.options: (a) publisher verification only; (b) admin-consent link plus in-app ask-your-admin card; (c) also split personal-use scopes (Files.Read, Calendars.Read, Contacts.Read) from org-sync scopes (Sites.Read.All, ChannelMessage.Read.All, Mail.Send in the default connect); (d) also lighten the Microsoft login scopes.
owner_decisions.recommended: Do (a), (b) and (c); decide (d) before onboarding the first non-admin business tenant. (c) is the cheapest way to let non-admin users connect personal tools. Under the default policy the repo's research says self-consent to Calendars.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All and Sites.* is blocked, and the login and the default Microsoft connect already request admin-only-looking scopes; verify each permission in Microsoft's table on a real tenant before settling.

owner_decisions.question: D4. Calendar invitations: may Verevon create or change events that have attendees?
owner_decisions.options: (a) no attendees in v1; (b) allow with a second explicit confirm that lists recipients; (c) allow freely.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). Graph sends invitations on create, so an event with attendees is an outbound email to third parties; Google needs sendUpdates and is handled the same way. Offer 'copy event details' instead. Revisit (b) once D1 data exists.

owner_decisions.question: D5. Widen the model-execution service principal with integration:write (ingestion audience only).
owner_decisions.options: (a) grant it; (b) keep it read-only and move all provider writes behind a new dedicated presenter principal.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). Without it no agent or worker provider write can mint a token (Control Plane policy lines 238-263). The real gates are the signed attestation bound to the exact payload, the owner-only check on the attestation actor, the idempotent action receipt and now always-ask; the exchanged delegated token still never mints write (contract spec keeps that). Needs a security reviewer and a launcher run to take effect.

owner_decisions.question: D6. Where do files go and when may Verevon overwrite?
owner_decisions.options: (a) new file in OneDrive > Verevon, rename on conflict, replace-original only for a file picked from OneDrive with an eTag guard and a second confirm; (b) always ask for a folder; (c) overwrite by name.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). Google: drive.file create only (no restricted drive scope). SharePoint team sites and shared drives stay out of v1 as already ruled for the picker (connector-picker.md section 6.1).

owner_decisions.question: D7. Google scopes for Sheets and Drive writes.
owner_decisions.options: (a) spreadsheets (sensitive) for Sheets edits plus drive.file for new files; (b) drive.file with the Google Picker for per-file grants; (c) full drive scope.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). Reads need no new scope (drive.readonly already covers Sheets reads; confirm). Needs the owner to confirm Google OAuth consent-screen verification status and lead time (not evidenced in the repo); avoid (c), it is a restricted scope.

risks: Cross-workstream dependencies are named by capability (Do mode on the Terra route, delegated-identity activation, the internal/api test compile fix, plan-gate approvals) because the A-F, H-J letter mapping was not in my brief. G does not depend on any of them except for the Do-mode agent paths and live proof of code_interpreter on Terra.

No agent provider write can succeed today: model-execution cannot mint integration:write (policy lines 238-263), and both the live loop and the cold worker call it. This also means mail.send through the agent has probably never run. Verified by reading policy and the mint path, not by running.

Chat Do runs self-approve provider writes under the auto posture. If G8's always-ask is not shipped together with the new write ops, the first enabled write would run without a pause. Keep the new capabilities un-requested (G7 dark) until G8 is deployed.

Reconnect overwrites capabilities today; until G1 lands, any surface that reconnects with default bundles silently removes granted write capabilities. The control-plane fallback refresh mints tokens from auth-core's app registration, which lacks write scopes, so a recorded write capability can still hit a provider 403 (mapped to reconnect_required).

Size ceilings: tonic 4 MiB, Fiber 4 MiB, axum 2 MB. Files are capped at 2.5 MB raw in v1 (staging, save, replace). Raising it means explicit max message sizes on gRPC and HTTP in four services, or content references instead of inline base64.

Unknown: whether ExecuteStep accepts steps on a completed run, what it persists of tool_input (must not store file bytes), and whether capability-core allows cap.tool.provider.execute (the ledger marks it source_only). G9's spike answers this before any UI work; the fallback is a per-apply run.

Vendor behaviour taken from memory of Microsoft and Google documentation, not verified in this read-only pass; each must be confirmed on a real account early: Graph workbook sessionless PATCH persistence and the roughly 5 MB range payload limit; PUT /drive/root:/path:/content creating parent folders and conflictBehavior=rename; If-Match on content PUT; event timeZone naming (IANA vs Windows); Graph event create sending invitations; prompt=admin_consent on the v2 authorize endpoint vs the /adminconsent endpoint with .default (the latter grants every permission on the registration, including write); which delegated permissions the default consent policy lets users grant (Files.ReadWrite, Contacts.Read); Sheets values.get accepting drive.readonly; Google sensitive vs restricted scope tiers.

Prompt-injection exfiltration through writes: a model that read a malicious document could write =WEBSERVICE/IMAGE/IMPORTDATA formulas, links in event bodies, or file names. The deny-list, plain-text rendering, server-built summaries and hash-bound approvals are required controls, enforced in Go and Rust from shared test vectors (drift test), not UI-only.
Graph and Google event creation with attendees is an outbound email to third parties; v1 blocks attendees (D4). Delete/update of an event that already has attendees sends cancellations.

Fidelity: python-pptx round-trips unknown parts but openpyxl drops charts and some features; the part-level fidelity check cannot see visual or conditional-formatting loss, so say 'N parts missing' not 'unchanged'. Live proof uses real Excel to open the result.

Terra specifics: code_interpreter has no live record on Terra (every record is Verevon Balance), image attachments are not sent on the subscription route, Do mode is disabled there, and the subscription usage cap was hit once (2026-09-29). Adding a tool changes the prompt for every turn, so G13 offers it only with a write-capable connection and runs the saved matrix once.

Consent and verification have owner lead time and cannot be built around: Microsoft publisher verification needs an MPN id and verified domain on both app registrations; Google sensitive-scope verification is not evidenced in the repo; a business test tenant with a non-admin member and an admin is needed for G11. I cannot create accounts or enter credentials; the owner must perform each connect.

Receipts: both Go and Rust extractors only match a string 'id'/'ts'; any write op that returns none (range PATCH, DELETE 204) would never reach Completed or verified in the cold worker, as with mail.send. G7 makes a string id mandatory per op.
Two Microsoft app registrations (auth-core sign-in and integration-corev2 connector) and a control-plane token fallback make 'which registration holds which scope' easy to get wrong; G12 records it.

ZDR and temporary chat: approval continuation descriptors refuse ZDR runs, so agent writes are blocked there by design; the click path must also refuse ZDR orgs server-side and temporary chat client-side (the BFF cannot see the temporary-chat flag, same as the picker).

Stale or missing docs: integration_tools.rs cites docs/actions-surface-operations.md, which does not exist; the CATALOG const is the source of truth and its descriptions still say mail search is unimplemented.

designs.goal: A user action in /chat (and on Home 'Hent ut') starts a durable run in Verevon's own hosted, governed Chromium. The run gets a real broker-issued grant with a broker-owned domain policy. A real model planner drives it, on the user's ChatGPT Terra subscription route, never Balance, in tests. It stops at risk-classified approvals. Its result lands in the thread. The user can watch it in the chat panel and take over. The user's own Chrome stays out. designs.current_state:
All of this is by reading; nothing was run. The audit's headline holds, but the real picture is worse. A grant issuer is only the second of four blockers, and the browser run is not Do mode, so it CAN be proven live on Terra once these are fixed.

BLOCKERS FOR AN AGENT-DRIVEN RUN
1. The start path fails earlier than the audit says. No code anywhere sends `x-browser-authorization` (a repo-wide search finds it only in model-gateway/execution-core auth code and their tests). The BFF `start_ai_run` (apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs:1263-1382) never mints it. `proxy_model_json_with_delegations` (chat/shared.rs:629-692) has no browser slot. model-gateway's `browser_run_start` (browser_run.rs:297-306) extracts `VerifiedBrowserBearer`, whose extractor returns 401 when the header is absent (auth.rs:401-413). So today POST /v1/browser/runs ends 401, not 403. The 403 is the next failure: `grant_id` is "session:{id}" (browser.rs:1235), and the broker mints random hex ids, so ValidateGrant never matches (resolve_browser_grant, browser_run.rs:138-202).
2. The broker is an island and a thin one. Nothing calls AcquireGrant. Grants are in memory (grant.go:62-70) with a fixed 15-minute TTL (server.go:22) and no sweep. The broker has no policy source: AcquireGrant normalizes whatever domains the caller sends (server.go:61), so "broker-owned domain policy" does not exist yet. The BFF `create_session` also sends no grant. In a dev stack that is invisible, because quarry-edge uses NoopGrantValidator when no validator URL is set (quarry-edge main.rs:1479). With ENVIRONMENT=prod quarry-edge requires grants (main.rs:182-196, agent_routes.rs:1377-1383). That would break manual hosted-browser sessions too. The registry has no browser-broker audience for quarry-edge (Control Plane config/plane-service-principals.json: audiences ["data-plane"]), and Quarry's gRPC validator only gets a bearer under dev-bypass (quarry-runtime grpc/browser_broker.rs:75-80).
3. The planner is off. `QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM=1` is set nowhere (not in Model Plane deploy compose, .env or the launcher). `LlmPlanner::from_env` therefore returns None (llm_planner.rs:93-99), and the loop runs the deterministic planner, which only emits Observe (browser_agent.rs:828-829). The July live proofs used the URL-marker login classifier, not a model (browser-workspace-hitl.spec.ts says so in its comments).
4. The planner cannot use Terra. It defaults to `verevon-balance`, the paid route (llm_planner.rs:65). Its InferRequest (llm_planner.rs:160-182) has no provider_hint and no subscription_connection_id. The governed agent loop explicitly refuses a subscription connection (agent.rs:1069-1072).
5. The run fails silently and delivers nothing. A planner error falls back to Observe (browser_agent.rs:840-843), so a usage-limit refusal or an expired token yields a 'completed' run that did nothing. `done` discards the model's answer (llm_planner.rs:250 returns None; browser_agent.rs:836-838 'agent reported task complete'). The tool output has no findings (tool_bridge/mod.rs:801-807). model-gateway terminalizes metadata-only on purpose (session_flow.rs:1195-1198). Nothing reaches the chat thread.
6. Delegated bearers live 300 s. The BFF mints one per request (audience_tokens.rs, no cache). The planner holds its inference bearer for the whole run and inference-core verifies it on every Infer call. Runs are therefore bounded to roughly 240 s.

BLOCKERS FOR LIVE VIEW AND TAKEOVER FROM /CHAT
7. The agent's Quarry run is owned by the service principal `service:execution-core`. Quarry authorizes by actor equality (agent_routes.rs:474-486), so the user's BFF frame, tabs and control routes cannot reach it. chat-run-watch.ts:449-452 hard-codes sessionId undefined, so BrowserChrome shows per-step artifact screenshots only. Quarry's step endpoint ignores control mode (the 409 'human takeover active' lives only in the BFF run_action, browser.rs:705-714). The execution-core loop never consults it. The chat panel's `liveRunId` only fires for plan-mode or research turns (use-chat-controller.ts:403-421). Approval cards bind to an assistant turn whose runId matches (refreshApprovalsForRun, :2012-2022).

WHAT ALREADY WORKS AND IS REUSED
- The manual hosted browser (BrowserChrome, WS frames, tabs, control chip).
- The in-loop risk gate with orchestration approvals and approval cards in the panel.
- Pause, resume and stop (control_ai_run, ChatLiveRunPanel.tsx:531-564).
- The step-screenshot console.
- The message-menu action pattern ('Planlegg dette', ChatMessages.tsx:781).
- `append_assistant_message_authenticated` (session_flow.rs:1302).
- The Terra test helper `requireProductSubscription` (tests/e2e/product-subscription-route.ts).
- A mock-broker test pattern (`TestBrowserBroker` in browser_run.rs tests).

WINDOW SHARE
Only a one-shot `getDisplayMedia` frame exists (DashboardComposer.tsx:1862-1895). It is wired at :3617, has no test, and has no live record. The subscription route cannot take images at all: the provider reports supports_vision=false, and normalize.rs:186-205 rejects attachments on that route.

DEPLOY NOTE
broker, model-gateway and execution-core are Model Plane (launcher stack index 2). The BFF ships with the frontend stack, and rebuilding it restarts the frontend container.

owner_decisions.question: D-E1. What domain scope does a hosted-browser run get, and who owns the policy?
owner_decisions.options: (a) hard fence = start-URL host plus domains the user lists in the run dialog; (b) fence plus an org allow-list from Control; (c) open web with a deny-list and approval on cross-domain hops only.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), with the broker as authority. A broker deny-list (platform hosts, internal suffixes) and a cap of 8 domains for chat-started runs. Leaving the fence stops the run with a clear message, and widening means a new run. Per-org policy from Control is a later step (b).

owner_decisions.question: D-E2. May a browser run's answer be written into the chat thread?
owner_decisions.options: (a) write the planner's result plus source URLs as an assistant message (non-ZDR only); (b) keep browser content out of history and show it only in the live panel.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). It is the same retention class as a web-search answer. Never store raw page text; ZDR and temporary chats are already refused.

owner_decisions.question: D-E3. May the browser planner run on the user's own ChatGPT subscription connection?
owner_decisions.options: (a) yes, only when the user selected that route, default stays verevon-balance for everyone else; (b) never, planner stays on Balance.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). It follows the explicit-choice rule chat already uses, and it is the only way to prove the loop live under the Terra-only rule. Set it to Balance only by explicit selection.

owner_decisions.question: D-E4. How does the user own the agent's browser so the chat panel can show it and take over?
owner_decisions.options: (a) run it with the user's delegated aud=quarry bearer (new x-quarry-authorization hop, no change to Quarry authorization); (b) let a service principal act on a user-owned Quarry run by presenting the broker grant as the delegation proof (needs owner_id on ValidateGrantResponse and a Quarry authorization change).
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). It is the repo's existing delegated-bearer pattern and needs no change to Quarry's authorization core. Cost: the run is bounded by the 300 s bearer lifetime, hence the 240 s clamp. A renewable credential for longer runs is a separate later decision.

owner_decisions.question: D-E5. Allow a Do-mode test route so the model-initiated browser_agent tool (E12), plan gate and wide research can be proven live?
owner_decisions.options: (a) allow Do mode on the subscription route for tests; (b) allow a bounded Balance budget for Do-mode tests; (c) keep both off and ship E12 unproven behind a flag.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) if the broker's tool-proposal protocol can carry the agent loop; otherwise (c). Build E12 only after this is ruled. The chat bridge (E9) already serves the user need and is provable now.

owner_decisions.question: D-E6. Continuous window share: build it, and under which rules?
owner_decisions.options: (a) keep paste and one-shot only; (b) opt-in share on send (E14); (c) timed continuous streaming.
owner_decisions.recommended: (b), with no retention of frames, blocked for ZDR and temporary threads, vision-capable non-subscription routes only, a visible Stop banner, and an org kill switch. Defer (c) until per-frame cost caps and retention rules exist. State clearly that the Terra route cannot show frames to a model.

risks: The Terra subscription cap was hit on 2026-09-29. The owner's own record puts the next live proof at the reset on 2026-10-03 17:45 UTC. Every planner step is one Codex call, so a proof run costs real quota. Keep it to 3 runs of 8 steps or fewer. Code and unit-test work can proceed before the reset, and the honest-failure path (Spec C) can be proven now.
The Codex output-schema mode may reject the planner's optional-field schema, or return fenced prose. E3 is a deliberate first spike for this; E4's strict-schema choice depends on it.

Delegated bearers last 300 s and the planner reuses one inference bearer for the whole run. Without the 240 s clamp and the fail-closed rule, a long run would silently degrade into Observe loops. The clamp must stay until a renewable credential exists (D-E4).

Today a planner failure is indistinguishable from success (silent Observe fallback). Changing it to fail closed will make existing manual 'AI-loop' runs fail visibly on a route problem. That is correct but user-visible; keep the Norwegian message plain.

The broker is in memory with fixed 15-minute grants. A broker restart invalidates in-flight runs, so the run fails with a clear 403. Durable grants are not in scope. Add the sweep, or the map grows without bound.

The domain fence is the only hard guard. The keyword risk classifier is a heuristic and the planner reads untrusted page text, so prompt injection can steer actions inside the allowed domains. E4 adds a 'page text is untrusted' line; it does not remove the risk. Per-action approvals on login, checkout, posting and destructive actions remain the backstop.

capability-core evaluates cap.browser.open (seeded high in migration 0008) before the permission layer (capability_policy.rs:793). The July runs passed it, but confirm the decision is allow and not ask during the E5 smoke; do not assume.

If Quarry enforces the manual session's stored constraints (max_steps 12, 120 s, single host from create_session) on an attached run, attaching an agent to a manual session would be cut off early. This is why E10 gives the agent its own user-owned run instead of attaching.

Prod is blocked independently of this work: the Control registry gives quarry-edge no browser-broker audience, and Quarry's gRPC validator only has a bearer under dev-bypass. The dev stack hides it because it uses NoopGrantValidator. E11 covers it and needs a security review.

The PlanConfig change touches 5 struct literals (including the ignored e2e test), and the BrowserRunStartRequest literal in model-gateway tests. The BFF image ships with the frontend stack, and rebuilding it restarts the frontend container while another session holds uncommitted frontend edits. Coordinate, or verify the BFF on a host preview first.
The window-share and Do-mode items cannot be proven live under the standing rule. Report them as built-and-unit-tested at best, never as parity.
ZDR and temporary threads are refused by browser runs (browser_run.rs:307-314). The bridge must show that as a stated reason, not a silent disabled button.

Defects found by reading:
- (a) Data loss on retry. handler.go:107 records the Postmark MessageID in an in-memory guard before alias resolution and before Gateway.Ingest. A 503 (the current state) then makes Postmark retry. Retries at 1, 5, 10, 10, 10 and 15 minutes fall inside the 30-minute TTL (main.go:200), hit 'duplicate', and get a 200 and are dropped for good. Postmark's documented schedule is 10 retries from 1 minute up to 6 hours, and a 403 stops retries. The comment at replay.go:8-18 claims 'never a correctness gap', and no test covers failure-then-retry (handler_test.go:186-201).
- (b) Possible silent mass-drop. postmark.go:107-143 derives the SPF/DKIM verdict only from an `Authentication-Results` header. Postmark's inbound docs list X-Spam-Status, X-Spam-Score and X-Spam-Tests (tokens such as SPF_PASS, DKIM_VALID_AU) and document no Authentication-Results header. If a real payload lacks it, every real email derives 'none' and is dropped with a 200. The fixtures are synthetic.
- (c) Raw HTML. When TextBody is empty, the HtmlBody is forwarded raw (handler.go:163-168), with no body cap below the 20 MB BFF limit.

Attachments: extraction needs an imports-core RS256 'ingestion' JWT that integration-corev2 cannot mint (attachments.go:70-95). Phase 1 can be text-only, with filenames listed.

Postmark is a new sub-processor of forwarded-email content. Region and DPA are unconfirmed, and it is absent from the compliance pack and the Trust Center.

owner_decisions.question: Mail-to-task v1: when is the draft produced?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Run on open: the email becomes a thread with the framed first turn, and the user presses 'Lag utkast' (one draft-only Ask turn on their own Terra route). (b) Unattended: a draft exists before the user opens the thread, which needs D10's unattended owner identity and a security review.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) for v1. It needs no new identity, no paid spend and no unattended model call, and it can be proven on Terra. Build (b) as J6 only after D10 passes its security review. State plainly that v1 creates a thread and a prompt to draft, not an unattended draft.

owner_decisions.question: Receiving domain, ingress and Postmark setup shape (provider is already ruled: Postmark, self-forward only).
owner_decisions.options: A dedicated subdomain (for example tasks.<your domain>) with MX to Postmark inbound on its own Postmark Server, versus reusing a main-domain address. Ingress: a path-restricted tunnel or reverse proxy to integration-api for /api/v1/webhooks/mail-task/postmark only, versus exposing the whole service. Webhook auth is Basic credentials embedded in the webhook URL (verify.go:11-24).
owner_decisions.recommended: A dedicated subdomain, its own Postmark Server, a path-restricted public route for that one path only, and a webhook secret of at least 32 random characters held in the launcher secret store. Pilot on your own org and your own verified address first. The domain name is your choice.

owner_decisions.question: Postmark is a new sub-processor of forwarded email content. Who may use mail-to-task, and when?
owner_decisions.options: Owner org only until the sub-processor list, transfer assessment and /trust page include Postmark and its region and DPA status are confirmed; versus enabling for all non-ZDR orgs now.
owner_decisions.recommended: Owner org only. user-core already refuses ZDR orgs. Enable for customer orgs only after Postmark (region, DPA, SCCs) is in docs/compliance/subprocessor-list.md, transfer-assessment.md and /trust, and counsel has seen it.

owner_decisions.recommended: (a) for v1; extraction is a separate small follow-up. xlsx and pptx stay unextracted until workstream H's H1 and H10 land.

owner_decisions.question: Notification when an email thread is created.

owner_decisions.recommended: Skip in v1. The thread appears in the /chat sidebar with a 'Fra e-post' badge (J5). Add the notification with J6, when a real draft exists, so it never says 'drafted' without a draft.

owner_decisions.question: Order and scope of third-party assurance.
owner_decisions.options: Counsel review, external pentest, ISO/IEC 27001 (Norwegian market norm) with ISO/IEC 42001 in the same cycle, SOC 2 Type I then II, or any subset.
owner_decisions.recommended: 1) Commission counsel review of docs/compliance now (it gates everything customer-facing). 2) Commission an external web-app and API pentest including multi-tenant tests, with a published summary. 3) Engage a compliance-automation platform and a certification body for ISO 27001 scoped to the platform, adding ISO 42001 once the management system exists (it matches the Trust Center's stated spearhead). 4) SOC 2 only when a US customer asks. Choose the vendors and budget yourself; engineering provides the J15 packet.

owner_decisions.recommended: Adopt that rule. The defensible sentence today is 'residency and ZDR are enforced per request on the routes that support them; no third-party certification yet'. Approve the J13 diff before it goes public.

owner_decisions.recommended: Always shown as one small line, from server-stamped values only, hidden when unknown. Label the ChatGPT-subscription route 'global' with the plain no-EU, no-ZDR wording, because that is what the code says (codex_subscription.rs:607-626).

owner_decisions.question: Customer-managed keys, self-host and sovereign offer.

owner_decisions.recommended: Build nothing now. State it in the limits page. Revisit when a signed contract requires it. The J15 memo gives the options and a rough scope.

The repo evidences a local Docker stack and production compose overrides but no deployment record, while docs/compliance and /trust say EU/EEA Azure hosting. Until stated, the limits page describes the environment as it is and /trust makes no claim beyond the evidence.

owner_decisions.recommended: Treat it as a defect (J16), and until fixed say in the limits page that per-user erasure of conversation content is not evidenced end to end.

risks: Data loss on retry (J1): while MailTaskPipeline is None the endpoint answers 503, and the replay guard turns Postmark's retries into silent 200 drops for 30 minutes. Do not enable the Postmark webhook before J1 lands.

Silent mass-drop (J2): the SPF/DKIM verdict reads a header Postmark does not document. Real mail could be dropped with a 200 and no visible error. The rule must be pinned on a real redacted payload, and the content-free diagnostic must ship with it.
Mail-task would 'work' invisibly: mail_task threads are excluded from /chat history and transcripts (history.rs:189-194, 350-353, 213). J5 is a hard part of Phase 1, not polish.

Prompt injection and memory poisoning from forwarded content: the body is untrusted even though the sender is the owner (self-forward). The mitigation is a draft-only, tool-less turn with memory save and connectors off. The server-side enforcement point by thread origin on the invoke path is not yet identified (J5 spike). A client flag alone is not enforcement.

New sub-processor: Postmark handles forwarded email content. Its region, DPA and SCC status are unconfirmed here. Enabling for customer orgs before the sub-processor list, transfer assessment and /trust include it would itself be an unsupported claim.

Shared files and proto: sessions.proto, the pb files, http_routes.rs and docker-compose files are shared with other workstreams. Use the proto steward and one regenerate batch, re-read before every edit, never revert others' hunks. Rust builds reliably only in Docker. A BFF rebuild restarts the frontend container (OD20), so batch it at a wave end after a git status check.

Standing rule on live tests: the mail-task live proof uses one or two Terra Ask turns only. Nothing here may route through Verevon Balance. Unattended drafting (J6) is blocked precisely because it would otherwise need a non-Terra route.
The public /trust page may already be live and may now be wrong in both directions (undisclosed subscription route, TTS line, tooltip). Narrow first. Its deployed state is unknown here.

The compliance pack and this evidence are by reading, not running. Several code comments are stale (gdpr_nats.rs, privacy.rs). Every evidence doc must say so, carry file:line, and pass the citation checker; unverified rows must stay marked UNVERIFIED.

Legacy Codex prompt logs (full prompts and attachments back to 21 Sep) may still exist on the integration-codex-subscription-home volume. Deleting them is permanent and owner-only; agents never do it.
Per-user erasure may not reach session-core or cost-core (initial reading). Until J12 and J16 settle it, no document may state that user erasure is complete.

Hosted-webhook exposure: Postmark needs a public HTTPS endpoint into a stack that today runs on a Windows PC. Restrict the route to the single path, keep the Basic secret out of chat and logs, and rate-limit (the receiver already does, plus the BFF per-user limiter).

J7 portability: the harness is macOS-flavoured (stat -f) and heavy. On Windows the 0600 check cannot pass, so either skip it with a warning or use WSL or Linux. It builds from the working tree, which holds other sessions' uncommitted edits, so a failure may not be this work's.

Assurance has external lead times (counsel, pentest vendor, certification body, an observation window for SOC 2 Type II). Nothing engineering does shortens them; the plan only removes our own delays and false claims.

Captions are descriptive text on silent video. Without the J9 text alternative the public player does not give screen-reader users an equivalent. The owner's visual and editorial review cannot be automated, and the manifest status stays blocked until the owner signs.
designs.live_proof:
Rule: Terra only (gpt-5.6-terra via openai-codex-subscription); never Verevon Balance or another paid provider. Counts and ids only; never tokens, message content, header values or payloads.

FREE, NO MODEL (can run as soon as the code exists)
1. J1/J2 unit tests: failure then retry reaches Ingest again; a forged duplicate auth header fails; HTML is stripped and capped. `go test ./internal/mailtask/... -race` is green.
2. J3: `docker compose config` resolves for the four compose files with fake values; the policy contract spec is green; the launcher dry run with fake credentials shows only the two new principals gain keys; check-mail-task-bindings.sh reports 'feature off' with nothing set.
3. Webhook negative probes against the running integration-api, after the owner sets the three switches: a wrong or absent Basic secret gives 401 and an unconfigured provider gives 404; a wrong To-domain gives a 200 drop; a gateway outage gives 503 and a later retry of the same MessageID within 30 minutes succeeds (J1). The logs show reason codes only.
4. J4/J5 mocked end to end: session-core against disposable Postgres creates one thread and one message, and a replay creates none; history and transcript include mail_task and exclude space, support, agent_run and system.

AFTER OWNER SETUP (about two Terra calls)
5. The owner sends one real forward from their own verified address to their alias: Postmark, the webhook (accepted), the bridge, and the thread appears in /chat with the 'Fra e-post' badge and banner. The owner shares only the redacted header block (names) so J2 pins the fixture.
6. A second delivery of the same MessageID (Postmark redelivery or re-forward test) returns the same thread id with one first-turn message.
7. A forged From (not the owner's verified email) and a mail from a different sender to the alias create no thread (reason sender_not_verified, no bounce).
8. The owner presses 'Lag utkast': exactly one Terra Ask turn, draft-only, tools off. The evidence is the served model, route, cost basis 'subscription', zero requests to any non-subscription provider in the inference-core log, and no cost-ledger rows. J14's line reads 'global'.
9. Record a dated row in the gap plan and the readiness record: counts and ids only. If Terra reports a usage cap, record it and stop; never switch model.

OTHER ITEMS
10. J7: the harness prints its PASS line with 2/2 browser cases; cleanup leaves no project resources; the manifest 'trust' gate flips only on that evidence plus the current-build memory and connected specs.
11. J8: previews export without error; the review sheet lists cues, durations and checks; the owner signs per film (not machine-checkable). The manifest status remains blocked until all gates and approvals are done.
12. J10-J13, J15: check-citations.mjs passes over docs/compliance/evidence; a second reader re-opens every cited file:line; the posture script's output contains no value outside its allow-list.
owner_checklist: Decide the mail-to-task questions: run-on-open versus unattended (recommended: run-on-open for v1), attachments (recommended: filenames only), notification (recommended: skip in v1), and who may use it (recommended: owner org only until Postmark is on the sub-processor list).
State, in one line, where customer data is hosted in production today and in which region. The compliance pack and /trust claim EU/EEA Azure hosting, and the repo has no deployment record.

Confirm whether the legacy Codex prompt logs (logs_2.sqlite and the legacy session transcripts on the integration-codex-subscription-home volume) have been deleted. If not, delete them yourself once the smoke turn shows no new logs file. Permanent deletion is owner-only; agents never do it.
Approve a quiet run window for the disposable cross-tenant harness (J7). No passwords are needed. Install any missing tool it reports (docker, pnpm, openssl, grpcurl) yourself.

Commission Norwegian privacy-counsel review of docs/compliance using the J15 packet. Nothing customer-facing is counsel-reviewed today; the status table stays unchanged until counsel records a review.

Choose and engage the external pentest vendor and set its scope from the J15 draft. Decide the certification path, body and compliance platform (recommended order: counsel, pentest, ISO 27001 plus ISO 42001, SOC 2 only on US demand).
Approve or edit the J13 /trust page diff (public content). Narrowing edits first; hold any broadening until counsel and evidence exist.

Create the Postmark account and a dedicated Postmark Server for inbound. Choose the receiving subdomain, add the MX record to Postmark's inbound host, generate the webhook secret (at least 32 random characters) into the launcher secret store, and set the inbound webhook URL with Basic credentials pointing at a path-restricted public route to integration-api (/api/v1/webhooks/mail-task/postmark only). Confirm Postmark's region, DPA and SCC terms and give them to engineering for the sub-processor list. Never paste secrets into chat.

After J1, J2 and J3 are merged and tested, set MAIL_TASK_PROVIDER=postmark, MAIL_TASK_WEBHOOK_SECRET and MAIL_TASK_RECEIVING_DOMAIN in the stack's local secret store (names only; values never in chat).

Apply the policy batch through the Control launcher: it adds model-gateway-mail-task-bridge and verevon-gateway and the integration-mail-task-worker credential, and restarts auth-core. Run check-mail-task-bindings.sh to confirm every binding is present. Agents never apply security settings to the running stack.

Approve the image rebuild window (launcher only; model-plane-only for Model Plane images, and the BFF rebuild batched at a wave end after a git status check), because J4 and J5 change session-core, model-gateway, the BFF and the frontend.

Send one real test email from your own verified address to your alias, then one from a different address to prove it is dropped. Share only the redacted header block (header names) so J2 can pin the sender-verification rule. Press 'Lag utkast' on the created thread (the Terra proof).
Confirm the Codex usage window has room for the roughly two proof turns, and refresh the local test sign-in if the machine rebooted. If capped, record it and stop; never switch model.

Do the editorial and media review of the four films: watch each short film and raw file with the draft captions, edit the captions, and sign each film in the review sheet. Then set the manifest approvals yourself. The manifest status stays blocked until every gate and approval is done.

Decide the open product questions that follow from J12 and J14: the residency-line default (recommended: always shown, from server values only), and treating a per-user erasure gap as a defect if J12 confirms it.
